companies.name: Lizzyai
companies.description: Lizzy is a generative-AI platform for legal professionals, delivering a secure Gen AI workspace across all practice areas through both a web application and a Microsoft Word/Outlook add-in. It supports contract drafting, review, analysis, and proofreading, customizable legal workflows and playbooks, in-document citations, redlining and track-changes, and the handling of long, scanned, watermarked, and multiple documents. A multi-LLM approach routes each task to the most capable model, and firms can train a private model that embeds their own know-how. Built for enterprise IT with a zero-trust architecture, no training on customer data, PII anonymization, SSO via SAML and OAuth 2.0, and shared, VPC, or self-hosted deployment options.

companies.name: Lumafield
companies.description: Lumafield is a manufacturing technology company that builds accessible industrial X-ray computed tomography (CT) scanning hardware and AI-powered cloud analysis software. Its Neptune and Triton scanners pair with the Voyager cloud platform so engineers and manufacturers can inspect the inside of parts non-destructively, measure dimensions and GD&T against CAD, detect porosity, cracks, inclusions and wall-thickness defects, and automate inspection at production volume. Lumafield delivers CT as a unified hardware, cloud, and analytics system rather than a public developer API; this profile catalogs its public developer-adjacent surfaces (support/knowledge base, release notes, and an llms.txt documentation index) for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Molekule
companies.description: Molekule is a consumer air-quality hardware company that makes FDA-cleared HEPA air purifiers for homes and businesses. It sells direct-to-consumer through molekule.com, a Shopify-hosted storefront. While Molekule does not publish a traditional developer API, its store exposes a live agent-commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp, a Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint at /api/ucp/mcp for AI shopping agents, OpenID Connect buyer authentication via the Shopify Customer Account API, and published agent instructions at /agents.md and /llms.txt. This profile captures that machine-readable commerce surface for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Piper Inc.
companies.description: Piper (Piper Learning, Inc. / Piper LLC) is an educational-technology company that makes hands-on STEM learning kits — most notably the Piper Computer Kit, a buildable wooden computer that teaches circuitry and coding through Minecraft, and Piper Make, a browser-based platform for exploring electronics and Python. Its consumer storefront runs on Shopify and exposes an agent-commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile with an MCP endpoint plus Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect, letting AI shopping agents search the catalog, build carts, and check out with explicit buyer approval. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched from its live public agent/discovery surface.

companies.name: Replicant
companies.description: Replicant is an enterprise agentic customer service platform that automates high-volume contact center conversations across voice, chat, and messaging, and analyzes 100% of interactions for QA, compliance, and automation insights. Its two products — Conversation Automation and Conversation Intelligence — replicate top-performing human agents using a hybrid agentic-plus-deterministic architecture with human-in-the-loop escalation, and integrate with existing CCaaS, CRM, telephony, and ticketing stacks. Replicant is telephony-native, runs multi-region on Google Cloud, and is built for SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI, and GDPR requirements. It is sales-led with a private, partner-facing API rather than a public developer portal.

companies.name: Rocksalt
companies.description: Rocksalt is a B2B inbound and social-engagement platform, headquartered in Redwood City, California and founded in 2023 by Arjun Moorthy (CEO), Anita Moorthy (CMO), and Ajoy Sojan (CTO). The product helps founders, executives, and subject-matter experts build visibility and win business on LinkedIn and Reddit in roughly ten minutes a day: an AI-powered digest surfaces the industry conversations worth joining, suggests personalized comments grounded in the user's expertise, assists with post creation, and adds team collaboration workflows plus analytics and HubSpot CRM sync. Rocksalt raised seed funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners in 2025. It is a marketing SaaS application delivered through a web app rather than a public developer API; this profile was surfaced from the Lightspeed portfolio and enriched with the company's public identity and web properties.

companies.name: Shoptiques
companies.description: Shoptiques is an online marketplace that brings thousands of independently owned local boutiques online, letting shoppers discover unique, one-of-a-kind fashion and home decor from over 5,000 stores. Founded in 2012 by Olga Vidisheva, the business rebranded its merchant/POS arm as Material in 2023 while continuing to operate the Shoptiques consumer marketplace. The storefront at shoptiques.com now runs on Shopify and exposes a modern agent-facing commerce surface: a published llms.txt / agents.md, Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect + OAuth 2.0 authentication, and a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint for buyer-approved, agent-driven shopping and checkout.

companies.name: Simantic
companies.description: Simantic builds simulated hardware for embedded QA, modernizing embedded firmware development through hardware simulation designed for AI adoption in hardware engineering. Its platform emulates microcontroller (MCU) systems so engineers can inject sensor readings and observe how their firmware reacts over CAN, Ethernet, and BLE, running full firmware test suites in CI (for example GitHub Actions) on every push and pull request without physical boards. A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server lets AI agents step through firmware, inspect peripheral state, and replay scenarios against a simulated MCU, and a CLI drives simulations locally. Simantic offers private, self-hosted deployment so firmware and test data never leave a team's own servers. Founded in 2025, Simantic is a Y Combinator (Fall 2026) company.

companies.name: Tempus AI
companies.description: Tempus AI (NASDAQ: TEM) is a precision medicine company that has built one of the world's largest libraries of de-identified clinical and molecular data, paired with an operating system to make that data accessible for diagnostics and research, starting with cancer. Its products span genomic profiling (xT / xR), AI-enabled clinical tools (Hub, One, Next), the Lens real-world data and agentic AI platform for life sciences, cardiology and radiology AI (ECG-AI, Pixel), and a consumer health app (Olivia). Tempus does not currently publish a self-serve, documented public developer API; integrations are delivered through enterprise and EHR channels (HL7 / FHIR, e.g. Epic) under partner agreements.

companies.name: Thamarah Al-Jill Co LLC
companies.description: Thamarah Al-Jill Co LLC operates AMUSED Co (amusedco.com), a Saudi Arabia-based online marketplace for authenticated, curated pre-loved luxury — designer handbags and women's clothing from houses such as Louis Vuitton, Hermes and Chanel at up to 70% off retail. Under a "Resell, Rebuy, Relove" model, buyers shop verified second-hand pieces (backed by a one-year authentication money-back guarantee) and sellers list their own unused items; payment options include credit card, Mada and Tamara. The store is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is built on Shopify and is fully agent-native: it publishes an /llms.txt agent guide and implements the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) over an MCP endpoint, with Shopify Customer Accounts OpenID Connect for buyer authentication.

companies.name: Tradespace
companies.description: Tradespace is an AI-powered intellectual property management platform that combines IP management software, AI tooling, and on-demand patent attorneys in a single full-service patent practice. The platform spans the IP lifecycle across four products — Create (invention harvesting and disclosure, with Slack, Gmail, and Notion integrations), Protect (AI-assisted patent drafting and flat-fee prosecution with senior attorneys), Manage (portfolio management and board-ready reporting), and Commercialize (licensing campaigns, claims charts, and licensee identification). It serves corporations, universities, tech transfer offices, startups, law firms, and government agencies, is SOC 2 Type 2 compliant (Vanta trust center), hosts on Microsoft Azure with customer-private AI instances, and is a 500 Global portfolio company. The SaaS application runs at app.tradespace.io; no public developer API is published.

companies.name: Winc
companies.description: Winc is a direct-to-consumer online wine club and retailer (winc.com) offering curated, personalized wine subscriptions and single-bottle purchases matched to a member's palate profile. The winc.com storefront runs on Shopify and exposes a modern agentic-commerce surface: a hosted UCP (Universal Commerce Protocol) MCP endpoint, Shopify Customer Account API authentication (OpenID Connect), and published /llms.txt and /agents.md agent instructions that let AI shopping assistants discover the catalog, build carts, and drive buyer-approved checkout. Originally surfaced as a VC portfolio company and enriched from its public agent-facing surface by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

This profile was surfaced as an a16z / Trinity Ventures portfolio company and enriched from Zulily's real public agent-commerce surface.

companies.name: Aris Machina
companies.description: Aris Machina builds AI-powered industrial software for advanced manufacturing, describing its mission as delivering "industrial superintelligence" that unifies design, production, and operations through AI agents and a shared semantic knowledge model. Its products include Protos, an AI co-engineer for R&D teams that accelerates design validation and simulation; Gemba, shopfloor operational agents that provide real-time equipment diagnostics; and the Ontology Toolkit, a knowledge-integration layer that bridges data across MES, ERP, and PLM systems. Aris Machina serves batteries, biopharma, robotics, defense, and aerospace, and is backed by Earlybird. The company operates from Stockholm, Bangalore, and California. This profile was surfaced as an Earlybird portfolio company and enriched from public web sources; Aris Machina does not currently publish a public developer API surface, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs.

companies.name: Binocs
companies.description: Binocs is an agentic AI-powered due diligence and strategic advisory platform for financial professionals — private equity, consulting, corporates and portfolio companies spanning private credit, venture capital and venture debt. The SaaS product (app.binocs.co) automates deal sourcing and screening, investment memos and market assessment, financial statement analysis, growth strategy and pricing diagnostics, CRM integration, and sell-side documentation (CIM, teasers), promising decision-ready diligence in minutes at up to 90% lower cost than traditional consulting. Binocs is an Accel portfolio company with offices in Jersey City, NJ and Bengaluru, India. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

companies.name: Bloomfilter
companies.description: Bloomfilter is a process intelligence platform that gives enterprises end-to-end visibility, traceability, and control over how AI agents and humans execute software delivery work. It unifies data across development and design tools such as Jira, GitHub, Azure DevOps, and Figma into a structured, AI-enabled data stream and builds a connected process graph across the software development lifecycle. Teams use Bloomfilter to govern hybrid human-agent workflows through process mining, compliance monitoring, cycle-time analysis, and performance measurement, so leaders can see how work actually flows and where value is created or lost. The company is a Techstars portfolio company and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead for enrichment.

companies.name: CardinalOps
companies.description: CardinalOps is a cybersecurity company delivering agentic detection engineering for security operations centers (SOCs). Its Threat Coverage Optimization Platform continuously assesses detection posture across SIEM and EDR tools (Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Cortex, Elastic and others), maps existing detections to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, surfaces coverage gaps, and automatically remediates broken or noisy rules. The Agentic Fleet and Cardinal AI use large language models to extract atomic TTPs from threat intelligence and generate new, validated detection rules. CardinalOps is backed by Battery Ventures and serves enterprise SOC teams. It publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public developer-adjacent, security, and compliance surface.

companies.name: Cedar
companies.description: Cedar is a healthcare financial technology company whose patient financial experience platform unifies billing, payments, insurance coverage, and support for health systems, hospitals, and clinician-services groups. Its products include Cedar Pay (pre-visit, post-visit, and financing patient payments), Cedar Cover (benefits and financial assistance, including Medicaid enrollment), Cedar Support (AI-powered patient support and call-center automation via Kora AI), and Cedar Intelligence (a proprietary AI system for personalized patient engagement). Cedar reports having served over 50 million patients and processed billions of dollars in patient payments. The company is backed by a16z, Founders Fund, QED Investors, and SV Angel. Cedar publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or GitHub organization; this profile captures its public identity, legal, and security-posture surface.

companies.name: Databand
companies.description: DBND (Databand) is an open-source Python framework — a library, a set of APIs, and a CLI — for building, tracking, and observing data pipelines across data ingestion, preparation, ETL/ELT, and machine-learning workflows. It collects pipeline metadata (runs, metrics, dataframes, schemas) to give data-engineering teams a system of record for runs and to detect pipeline failures and data quality issues before they hit downstream consumers. The DBND SDK integrates with Apache Airflow, Apache Spark, Databricks, dbt, and IBM DataStage. Databand was acquired by IBM in 2022 and is now IBM Databand, part of IBM's data observability offering; the open-source DBND SDK remains published on PyPI and GitHub under the databand-ai organization.

companies.name: Fearn
companies.description: Fearn is the AI-native patent prosecution firm built for startups. It pairs former Big Law patent attorneys with proprietary, hallucination-resistant AI models built in-house by PhD computer scientists to take an invention from disclosure to a filing-ready provisional or non-provisional patent draft in minutes rather than the 50+ hours typical of traditional firms, at flat-rate pricing with automated labeled-figure generation and a money-back guarantee tied to claim allowance. Fearn self-hosts its entire AI infrastructure and uses no third-party model APIs, keeping invention disclosures confidential and compliant with SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27701, and GDPR. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in San Francisco; backed by Kindred Ventures and a16z speedrun. Fearn is a legal-services company and does not currently publish a public developer API.

companies.name: Fifteenth
companies.description: Fifteenth is a San Francisco-based fintech company operating an AI-powered personal tax platform for ambitious earners — founders, investors, executives, and technology professionals with complex financial situations such as equity compensation (ISOs, RSOs, RSUs, NSOs), liquidity events (IPOs and acquisitions), partnership income (K-1s), and active stock and crypto trading. The service pairs dedicated human CPAs with AI-driven automation: users link their banking, payroll, and investment accounts via one-click integrations (Workday, Rippling, Robinhood, Wealthfront, Carta, Charles Schwab, AngelList, Coinbase and more), and the platform automatically detects tax-relevant transactions, organizes documents, models scenarios, and delivers proactive quarterly planning plus unlimited year-round advice at flat-fee pricing starting around $1,000 per year. Fifteenth raised $8.25M in seed funding (February 2025) led by A* and General Catalyst. It is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and public web properties.

companies.name: Hallo
companies.description: Hallo is an AI-powered language assessment and language-learning company backed by Battery Ventures. Its enterprise platform delivers automated, AI-driven proficiency assessments across speaking, writing, listening, and reading in 80+ languages, with CEFR-aligned scoring, detailed feedback (fluency, vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, coherence), real-time score reports and dashboards, and proctoring / anti-cheating for high-stakes hiring, placement testing, and employee development. Hallo integrates with major applicant-tracking systems (Greenhouse, Ashby, Workday, SmartRecruiters, Lever, SuccessFactors, Recruitee, and others) and runs assessments across 160+ countries, with a stated SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, and EU AI Act compliance posture. The company also operates a consumer language-learning app with AI tutors and native-speaker practice. Hallo does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI specification; its integration surface is delivered through prebuilt ATS connectors and enterprise onboarding rather than a self-serve developer portal.

companies.name: Hopper
companies.description: Hopper is a travel marketplace and fintech, best known for consumer flight, hotel, car, and homes booking with fintech ancillaries such as Price Freeze, Cancel for Any Reason, and Disruption Assistance for Any Reason. Hopper Technology Solutions (HTS) is the B2B arm that exposes Hopper's e-commerce (Stays, Cars, Packages), fintech ancillaries, loyalty portals, and HTS Assist agentic AI to banks, airlines, and travel providers including Capital One, Air Canada, Virgin Australia, Tripadvisor, Frontier, Wizz Air, and Porter.

companies.name: Ixlayer
companies.description: Ixlayer is a direct-to-patient healthcare technology company that helps biopharmaceutical companies transform the patient experience through an integrated, AI-enabled platform. Its unified platform spans virtual patient onboarding and intake, telehealth for primary and specialty care, at-home and in-center lab testing with mobile phlebotomy, prescription fulfillment (retail, specialty, and home delivery), benefits verification and claims, connected care with provider directories and scheduling, and the ixAI patient concierge for AI-powered support and care coordination. Ixlayer says it has powered more than 1,100 nationwide programs and enabled over 4 million patient care journeys, and states its services are SOC 2 Type 2, HIPAA, and GDPR compliant. The company is backed by General Catalyst.

companies.name: Lunabill
companies.description: LunaBill is an AI revenue cycle management (RCM) platform for hospitals, health systems, and RCM/BPO firms, built by LunaHealth Technologies, Inc. and backed by Y Combinator. A coordinated team of AI agents works the entire accounts receivable queue end to end — placing real calls to payers and waiting on hold, navigating IVR phone trees, checking payer portals (Availity, Waystar), working denials, filing appeals, and resubmitting claims — while running inside the EHR and clearinghouses a provider already uses (Epic, Cerner, GoRev, Waystar, Availity) and leaving a full audit trail on every claim. Pricing is performance based (1.5% of net collections recovered, nothing upfront). LunaBill is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type I (Type II in progress). It does not currently publish a public developer API; integration is delivered through EHR and clearinghouse connectors rather than a documented API surface.

companies.name: Mimic
companies.description: Mimic is an enterprise cybersecurity company building ransomware and AI-threat defense based on "Known-Good Enforcement" at the kernel level. Its SaaS platform models a system's authorized state and blocks unauthorized modifications, detecting ransomware in fractions of a second to deflect attacks before they can encrypt data or damage infrastructure, and providing rapid-recovery technology that restores in seconds-to-minutes rather than days. Product lines include Ransomware Defense, AI Shield (Guard/Patch/Trace) and Agentic AI Governance. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, Mimic raised a $27M seed and a $50M Series A led by GV (Google Ventures) and Menlo Ventures, with Ballistic Ventures, Team8, Wing Venture Capital and Shield Capital participating; former Mandiant CEO Kevin Mandia joined its board. The platform is enterprise/government-facing (sold via demo, no public developer API) and is aligned with GDPR, SOC 1 & 2, IL4/IL5 and holds FedRAMP Ready status. Added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead.

companies.name: One Model
companies.description: One Model is an HR and people-analytics software platform that unifies fragmented workforce data from HRIS, ATS, payroll, engagement, performance, and finance systems into a governed data mesh, then applies AI to turn it into insights for HR leaders and executives. Its products include Data Mesh (unify, govern, and activate data across sources), Data Stories (dashboards and reporting), One AI (a transparent predictive-modeling pipeline plus a natural-language assistant), and enterprise AI connections — including an MCP Server Access option — that let governed people data feed tools such as ChatGPT, Copilot, and Claude with role-based access controls. One Model is ISO 27001:2022 certified and SOC 2 Type II attested, and adheres to GDPR data-processor requirements.

companies.name: Orolabs
companies.description: ORO Labs provides an agentic procurement orchestration platform for enterprise spend management. It coordinates people, processes, systems, and data so employees can get what they need without friction, unifying intake management, supplier onboarding and lifecycle, risk and compliance orchestration, and AI-driven workflow automation. The platform offers a no-code workflow builder, a purpose-built agent builder for custom procurement AI agents, and bring-your-own-LLM flexibility, with secure, semantically rich integrations across the procuretech landscape. ORO Labs is backed by Felicis and Norwest Venture Partners.

companies.name: Pango
companies.description: Pango is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building an AI-powered operating system for e-commerce post-purchase and logistics operations. The platform positions itself as an "agentic OS" — autonomous AI agents that handle back-office logistics tasks — and consolidates multi-carrier delivery management, checkout delivery options, branded order tracking, and returns processing into a single unified system. Pango advertises multi-carrier orchestration across 100+ shipping providers with AI-powered routing and rate optimization, self-service return portals with automated approvals, warehouse pick-and-pack automation, and AI agents that resolve exceptions and automate workflows. It integrates with major commerce platforms (Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Magento, Salesforce Commerce, NetSuite) and 100+ carrier, WMS, marketing, and support partners. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass the company markets an "API-first architecture" but publishes no public developer documentation, API reference, OpenAPI spec, or SDK.

companies.name: Slang Ai
companies.description: Slang AI is a voice-AI phone-answering and reservation platform for restaurants. Its customizable virtual phone agent answers every inbound call 24/7 in a natural, human-like voice, instantly responds to guest inquiries, and automatically manages reservations, with official integrations to OpenTable, SevenRooms, Tripleseat, Yelp, and Fishbowl. Founded by former Spotify data scientists, Slang AI reports 96%+ guest satisfaction (CSAT), 50% more phone reservations, and up to 200 staff hours saved per month. It is offered as a hosted SaaS product across Core, Premium, and Enterprise plans; at the time of profiling it exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal.

companies.name: Talentium
companies.description: Talentium is an end-to-end, AI-powered hiring platform that automates candidate sourcing, screening, and outreach so founders, in-house talent teams, and recruitment agencies can fill roles faster. It combines deep talent search across public sources (including technical talent on GitHub), your own network, and applicant pools with AI ranking, a unified candidate-communication inbox, interview assistance, branded career pages with job-board distribution, and ATS pipeline tracking — plus an autonomous hiring assistant ("Ted") and 60+ integrations. The platform is GDPR-compliant, hosted in EU data centers with end-to-end encryption, and is available on the Google Cloud Marketplace. Backed by EQT Ventures. This profile was enriched from the company's public web surface; Talentium publishes no public developer/API surface as of this pass.

companies.description: CoLab is an AI-powered design review platform for engineering and product-development teams. CoLab also publishes a REST-based Enterprise API (50+ endpoints) for two-way integration with PLM/PDM and other engineering systems — provisioning workspaces, users, and roles, importing files and feedback, and extracting review activity — with audit logging on every action. companies.name: Exaforce
companies.description: Exaforce is a security operations platform that pairs AI agents with a unified data layer to help teams detect, triage, investigate, and respond to threats faster. Its four autonomous "Exabot" agents (Detect, Triage, Investigate, and Respond) automate SOC workflows across 100+ data sources spanning cloud, identity, endpoint, SaaS, and code repositories, and can run as a self-operated platform or as a managed detection and response (MDR) service staffed by expert analysts working alongside the AI 24/7. Exaforce positions itself as an agentic-SOC alternative to traditional SIEM tooling while retaining integration compatibility. The company is backed by Mayfield and profiled in the API Evangelist network. No public developer API or reference documentation is currently published; this profile captures the company's public web, security, and trust surface.

companies.name: Fermat
companies.description: FERMÀT is an AI-native commerce platform that consolidates the shopper analytics, personalization, and experimentation stack into a single agentic system for direct-to-consumer and enterprise brands. It runs a closed loop — detect shopper behavior, recommend revenue-optimizing actions, generate adaptive storefront experiences and product pages, then feed performance signals back into detection — replacing tools like FullStory, Amplitude, Algolia, and Optimizely. FERMÀT integrates with ecommerce platforms including Shopify Plus, Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Adobe Commerce, and Oracle ATG via batch and streaming data syncs, and serves brands such as Glossier, GNC, Backcountry, AWAY, Travelpro, and TONAL. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures, Greylock, and QED Investors.

companies.name: Findem
companies.description: Findem is an AI Talent Intelligence platform that blends assistive AI for sourcing, marketing, executive search, and analytics with agentic AI workers for intelligent job posting, application boost, screening, and scheduling. The company also exposes Embedded AI building blocks (AI Job Board, Sourcing Copilot, Labeling Engine, Agents, and MCP) for partners to ship branded AI hiring experiences. Findem is sold enterprise-direct; ATS, HRIS, and partner integrations are gated rather than offered through a public self-serve developer portal.

companies.name: kelaHealth
companies.description: kelaHealth is a healthcare AI company that improves surgical outcomes through its Surgical Intelligence Service, an AI-enabled API delivering patient-specific predictive insights at critical decision points across the perioperative process. Models trained on millions of surgical procedures predict individual patient risk across nine major complication categories, identify modifiable factors, and recommend stratified interventions tailored to hospital standards. The service integrates into existing medtech and healthcare software applications using EHR, robotic, and social-determinants-of-health data to help providers improve growth, efficiency, quality, and safety. kelaHealth is HIPAA compliant and backed by Techstars. It does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs; its API is delivered through partner integrations.

companies.name: MelodyArc
companies.description: MelodyArc is an enterprise AI operations platform that orchestrates data, business rules, AI agents, and human workers in one governed system, so the right judgment is applied at the right moment, every time. It turns messy, cross-system, high-consequence operational work into modular building blocks: Points (atomic units of work capturing context, action, state, and ownership), Point Sets (reusable workflow configurations), a Point Engine (a dynamic decision graph routing tasks through rules, automation, AI, and human intervention in real time), AI Operators (configured workers with instructions and tools), a Portal for oversight and intervention, and Record for built-in traceability. It targets enterprise operations teams handling high-consequence work at scale and runs on managed or self-hosted infrastructure. Backed by Bloomberg Beta.

companies.name: PredictionIO
companies.description: Apache PredictionIO is an open source machine learning server that lets developers and data scientists build, deploy, and serve predictive engines as web services. It exposes a REST-based Event Server for collecting event data and an Engine Query API for real-time predictions, built on Apache Spark, MLlib, HBase, Elasticsearch, and Akka HTTP, with official SDKs for Python, Ruby, PHP, and Scala/Java. This profile enriches the original portfolio-lead stub.

companies.name: Sazabi
companies.description: Sazabi is an AI-native observability platform that helps engineering teams find and fix production issues faster. Autonomous agents watch application logs (stdout/stderr) to detect anomalies, unfamiliar errors, traffic spikes, and failed deployments without traditional dashboards, then deliver contextual, root-cause alerts into Slack and Microsoft Teams. Engineers investigate in natural language by mentioning the Sazabi agent, and the platform can hand off context to coding agents such as Claude, Cursor, and Codex or open pull requests to remediate. Sazabi instruments 35+ hosting providers with no code changes and exposes a hosted Sazabi MCP server so agents can query logs, inspect issues and projects, and discover Sazabi tools. Founded by Sherwood Callaway; part of the Y Combinator P26 (Spring 2026) batch; backed by an $8M seed round led by J2 Ventures, Village Global, and Y Combinator, with an open beta.

companies.name: Taito.ai
companies.description: Taito.ai is an AI-native people operations (HRIS) platform headquartered in Helsinki, Finland, built for teams scaling from roughly 30 to 300 employees. It unifies the employee lifecycle in one system — a people directory, time-off and attendance, documents and eSignatures, and performance reviews — alongside AI "people agents" that handle onboarding, reminders, payroll reporting, and policy questions on demand from Slack, Claude, or any MCP-compatible tool. Every platform action is exposed over the Model Context Protocol rather than a public REST API. Pricing is a single per-seat tier covering both the people-ops and performance modules. The company is ISO 27001 certified and GDPR compliant, publishing audit reports on a Vanta-hosted Trust Center, and raised a $2.7M seed round led by Accel.

companies.name: Ultromics
companies.description: Ultromics is a UK-based clinical AI company, spun out of the University of Oxford and backed by GV, whose EchoGo platform applies FDA 510(k)-cleared AI to routine echocardiograms to help clinicians detect heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and cardiac amyloidosis. EchoGo integrates into existing hospital echo workflows and PACS environments, delivering results through clinical systems rather than a public developer API.

companies.name: Enjamb Labs
companies.description: Enjamb Labs builds an AI-agent platform for pharmaceutical drug development. Its browser-based "integrated research environment" runs specialized agents across the full R&D lifecycle -- clinical evidence synthesis, trial design and statistical programming, and regulatory submission preparation -- while connecting to the systems pharma teams already use (Benchling, Veeva, Medidata, SAS) so no data migration is required. The workspace bundles Word/Excel/PowerPoint editors, Python and R compute environments, and 100+ scientific integrations, and emphasizes auditability, traceability, and human review, keeping each output attached to its sources, files, code, and decisions. Backed by Y Combinator and Founders, Inc., Enjamb reports early usage across major pharmaceutical companies including Johnson & Johnson, Merck, AbbVie, Bristol Myers Squibb, and Sanofi.

companies.name: Pulse Labs
companies.description: Pulse Labs is an AI-powered user experience research platform, founded in 2017, that helps product, design, and UX research teams gather and analyze real-world user feedback. The platform combines surveys, moderated and unmoderated interviews, task-based evaluations across web, mobile, smart devices, and automotive, and naturalistic observations, alongside its FlightRecorder SDK for embedded in-app feedback and session replay on iOS, Android, Web, React, and Flutter. Participant recruiting is powered by the proprietary Pulse Voices panel. Backed by Google, Amazon, Bezos Expeditions, Techstars, and Madrona Ventures, Pulse Labs emphasizes privacy, ethical AI, and enterprise-grade security including ISO 27001 certification and GDPR compliance. Pulse Labs does not currently publish a public REST API or OpenAPI; its developer-facing surface is the FlightRecorder embedded SDK and GitBook product documentation.

companies.name: ShopShops
companies.description: ShopShops is a livestream commerce marketplace for authenticated pre-owned luxury and designer goods — handbags, jewelry, watches, accessories, and shoes sold through live shopping events and an online store. Buyers shop curated secondhand inventory with authentication (via Entrupy), buy-now-pay-later (Afterpay / Shop Pay), and return assurance (Seel). The storefront runs on Shopify and publishes a live agent-commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile, an MCP endpoint for agent-driven catalog search and buyer-approved checkout, an OIDC/OAuth2 Customer Account API, and an llms.txt describing how AI shopping agents may transact with the store.

companies.name: Token
companies.description: Token Security is a cybersecurity company that secures non-human identities (NHIs) and AI agents across on-premises, hybrid, and cloud environments. Its platform continuously discovers every AI agent, service account, and machine identity, maps ownership and security posture, detects identity threats, and automates remediation. Capabilities span NHI inventory, security posture management, lifecycle management, secrets, and identity threat detection and response. The company also ships the Token MCP Server and a native Token AI Agent so security teams can query and act on NHI data conversationally from Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Cursor. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, GGV Capital, and Qiming, Token Security serves enterprise security teams, CISOs, and IAM professionals governing machine and agent identity at scale.

companies.name: AvoMD
companies.description: AvoMD (Avo) is a clinical AI platform that integrates directly with electronic health record (EHR) systems to power AI copilots for healthcare workflows. It combines EHR data with trusted clinical knowledge bases to support decision-making, documentation, and care delivery across inpatient and outpatient settings. Avo's product line includes Chart Assist, an AI Scribe for ambient clinical documentation, and AI Consult, serving rural and small hospitals, large and mid-size hospitals, and ambulatory care, in partnership with medical societies and knowledge partners. The company is SOC 2 Type II compliant and backed by 500 Global.

companies.name: Clarisights
companies.description: Clarisights is an enterprise marketing analytics platform that unifies marketing data from channels, web analytics, attribution platforms, and the data warehouse into a single self-service system. Marketing teams explore data, build custom dashboards, and generate trustworthy insights without SQL or data-engineering support, accelerating reporting cycles and reducing manual spreadsheet work. Clarisights also ships a Marketing Data MCP server that connects governed marketing data to AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and Gemini, exposing discovery, query, and report-navigation tools scoped by the same workspace access controls as the UI. The platform advertises 50+ connectors, ISO 27001 certification, and SOC 2 Type 2 attestation.

companies.name: Crogl
companies.description: Crogl is an enterprise AI security operations platform that deploys autonomous AI agents to investigate security alerts and threat advisories entirely within a customer's own infrastructure. Using a neurosymbolic approach that combines knowledge graphs, large language models, and security best practices, Crogl gathers context, queries existing security tools, and cross-references data across SIEM, EDR, ticketing, and data-lake systems without exfiltrating data. It is tool-agnostic — integrating with Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, CrowdStrike, ServiceNow, Jira, Databricks, Snowflake, Amazon S3, and Cribl — and every action is auditable so human analysts retain final decisions. Crogl is offered as a free single-user deployment and an enterprise plan with SSO, RBAC, and 24/7 SLAs. It is a Menlo Ventures portfolio company. Crogl does not currently publish a public REST API, OpenAPI specification, or developer SDK; its API surface (connectors) is part of the on-premises product.

companies.name: DataSnipper
companies.description: DataSnipper is an AI-powered, agentic productivity platform built specifically for audit, tax, and finance teams. It automates repetitive testing and analysis work - extracting, matching, and analyzing data across documents and systems - while keeping human professionals in control of final decisions. Capabilities include AI Agents for end-to-end workflows (revenue testing, tests of detail, royalty calculations), Excel Agents that run analysis directly inside spreadsheets, and document intelligence that collects and cross-references evidence. The platform serves external audit, internal audit, tax, financial control, government audit, and advisory teams, with a security-first posture (no training on customer data, encryption, and 24-hour document deletion). Backed by Index Ventures and Insight Partners.

companies.name: Entelo
companies.description: Entelo is an AI-powered talent-sourcing and recruiting-automation platform for finding, engaging, and hiring candidates using predictive analytics, diversity-aware search, and candidate-engagement tooling. Entelo was acquired and is now delivered as "Entelo Recruit" within Rival (rival-hr.com), an AI-powered HR orchestration suite spanning recruiting, workflow, learning, and performance. Its former domain entelo.com now 301-redirects to Rival. No public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI is currently published for the Entelo/Rival Recruit product.

companies.name: General Intuition
companies.description: General Intuition is a frontier AI lab building large action foundation models that can perceive, predict, and act across space and time in both virtual and physical environments. Spun out of the gaming clip platform Medal, the company trains its spatial-temporal reasoning models on billions of action-labeled gameplay clips - recordings of exactly which buttons a player pressed and when - to teach AI agents how to move through and reason about the world. Its Mira world model powers applications across games, simulation, and robotics. Founded in 2025 and based in New York City, General Intuition has raised $454M total, including a $320M Series A at a $2.3B valuation, and is onboarding first partners to a commercial API ahead of a broader developer release.

companies.name: Layla AI
companies.description: Layla is an AI travel agent that plans trips conversationally, generating itineraries with flights, hotels, activities, and restaurants wired into real booking inventory from partners such as Booking.com and Skyscanner. The consumer product is at layla.ai; a Layla for Brands white-label offering lets travel companies embed an AI travel agent into their own site with their own branding and inventory.

companies.name: Mosaic Ml
companies.description: MosaicML - now Databricks Mosaic Research - is a machine learning systems company that builds open-source tooling for training and deploying large neural networks and generative AI models faster and at lower cost. Its flagship open-source projects include Composer (a PyTorch library of training speedup methods), LLM Foundry (code for training and finetuning large language models), and Streaming (a library for streaming large datasets from cloud object stores into PyTorch training). MosaicML also shipped a managed training and inference platform driven by the mosaicml-cli (mcli) command-line tool; following the 2023 Databricks acquisition that platform is now offered as Databricks Mosaic AI. The company does not publish a standalone public REST/OpenAPI surface - its developer surface is Python packages, a CLI, and its open-source GitHub repositories.

companies.name: Packmind
companies.description: Packmind captures and governs your development playbook so every AI agent follows your rules consistently, across teams and repos. It helps teams maintain code quality and consistency standards.

companies.name: Paxton AI
companies.description: Paxton AI is a legal AI assistant built for attorneys and law firms, delivering rapid case-law and regulatory research, AI-assisted document drafting, file analysis, deposition and discovery summarization, and specialized workflows for medical chronologies and billing summaries. Founded by Tanguy Chau (CEO) and Michael Ulin and headquartered in Bend, Oregon, the company has raised roughly $28M across a $6M seed round led by WVV Capital and a $22M Series A led by Unusual Ventures, with participation from Kyber Knight and 25Madison. Paxton's platform covers US federal regulations, state laws, and case law across all fifty states, surfaces precise authority-linked citations, and runs in a closed model environment that is SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA compliant with data never used for model training. The product is delivered as a web SaaS targeted at solo practitioners, small and mid-size firms, and enterprise legal teams across personal injury, family, employment, criminal, and corporate practice areas; commercial access is sold via per-seat Individual plans ($499/month or $2,999/year) and a volume-priced Enterprise plan, with a 7-day free trial. Paxton publishes a small public GitHub presence with citator and legal-hallucination benchmark datasets but does not offer a public developer API, SDK, or open-source platform.

companies.name: Picnicai
companies.description: PicnicHealth (PicnicAI; legally Mission Health Labs, Inc.) is a San Francisco health-data company and Y Combinator alum (S14, founded 2014) that turns patients' fragmented medical records into structured, research-ready real-world datasets. Its consumer product gives patients a unified timeline of care across every provider, while PicnicResearch supplies de-identified, ontology-mapped (RxNorm, SNOMED, LOINC, ICD) real-world data to biopharma via AI extraction plus human clinical curation. The primary developer surface is a first-party R package distributed through PicnicHealth's own Posit/RStudio Package Manager for importing and visualizing research cohorts.

companies.name: Robocurve
companies.description: Robocurve is a San Francisco Public Benefit Corporation (Y Combinator Summer 2026) building open-source tools and independent benchmarks to help society understand what AI and robots can actually do in the physical world. Its flagship framework, Inspect Robots ("the Inspect AI for robotics"), runs any vision-language-action policy on any embodiment against any benchmark with full trace logs and live Rerun visualization, and integrates with ROS, Isaac Lab, and LeRobot. World Evals is its curated catalog of physical-world benchmarks (KitchenBench, DataCenterBench). Everything ships MIT-licensed as Python packages with a command-line interface rather than a hosted REST API.

companies.name: Zeroclick
companies.description: ZeroClick is the agent-first storefront and transaction layer that lets businesses sell directly to AI agents. It turns any existing API or offering into an agent-purchasable service, publishing a machine-readable storefront so agents can discover it and adding agent identity, agent-native payment rails (x402 and MPP, the Machine Payments Protocol), signed proxying, and per-transaction analytics in front of the seller's unchanged upstream API. Sellers keep their product, pricing, and customer experience, add a small guard to billed endpoints via the @zeroclickai/sellers SDK, and settle revenue to their own connected Stripe account. ZeroClick launched in July 2026, raised $55M, is backed by Forerunner Ventures, and is a product of the People's Internet Experiment.

companies.name: Appriss Retail
companies.description: Appriss Retail provides AI-powered solutions that help retailers manage Total Retail Loss across in-store and online channels. Its SaaS platform combines data intelligence, decision intelligence, and workflow intelligence to reduce returns fraud, shrink, and exceptions in real time. Marquee products include Appriss Engage (return and claims authorization, incorporating the Verify return-authorization engine), Appriss Secure (shrink and exception analytics), Appriss Incident (case management), Sidekick (an AI collaborator for loss-prevention teams), and the APIS performance-intelligence platform. Appriss Retail serves more than 60 of the top 100 U.S. retailers, drawing on 20+ years of retail data science. Programmatic integration is delivered to retailer clients through the APIS Online cloud portal rather than a public self-serve developer program.

companies.name: Base Ai
companies.description: Base is an AI Engagement OS for customer-led growth (CLG). The platform unifies advocacy, references, referrals, reviews, community, customer success, lifecycle engagement, and revenue attribution for B2B post-sale teams. Built for customer marketing, customer success, and RevOps teams, Base uses 100+ AI agents to automate onboarding, adoption, upsell/expansion, retention, and advocacy across the entire post-sale customer lifecycle, and to turn customer signals and feedback into references, testimonials, and expansion plays. Base integrates with Salesforce, HubSpot, Gainsight, Slack, and Zendesk, and is backed by Wing Venture Capital. Base does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API reference.

companies.name: Continuum
companies.description: Continuum (gocontinuum.ai) is an AI-powered platform that automates B2B returns, warranties, and repairs for distributors and manufacturers. It handles the post-sales workflow end to end through four solution hubs: a Customer Hub with self-service warranty and return portals, a Warehouse Hub for one-click receiving, inspection and dispute processing, a Vendor & Finance Hub for automated vendor engagement and accounts-receivable management, and a Manufacturer Warranty Hub for warranty claim automation. The company reports outcomes such as a 70% reduction in returns labor cost, a 30% increase in profitability, and an 8% reduction in customer churn. Continuum integrates with major distribution ERP systems (Infor, NetSuite, Epicor, Oracle, Acumatica). Based in Chicago, it is seed-funded and backed by Cowboy Ventures. Continuum is SOC 2 audited and publishes a public trust center. No public developer API or documentation is available at this time.

companies.name: Doctronic
companies.description: Doctronic is a consumer telemedicine platform that pairs an AI doctor with licensed physicians for anonymous, low-cost health care. Users describe their symptoms to an AI assistant that performs a free symptom assessment and health consultation, then can escalate to a real doctor for a video visit ($39/visit), prescription refills, lab orders, and follow-up care. Positioned as "Free. Anonymous. Built by doctors," the product is direct-to-consumer web and mobile rather than a developer platform: it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation. The only public machine-readable surface is an RFC 9116 security.txt with a coordinated vulnerability-disclosure policy. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Union Square Ventures.

companies.name: Native Security
companies.description: Native Security is a cloud security control plane that unifies security posture and enforcement across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and OCI. The platform translates security intent expressed in natural language into enforceable architectural controls, shifting teams from reactive detection toward proactive, secure-by-design defense using built-in cloud security primitives. Capabilities include multi-cloud policy enforcement from a single definition, automated organization topology discovery and mapping, architectural segmentation and perimeter enforcement, AI-agent guardrails through architectural boundaries, and compliance automation with audit readiness. Native Security is backed by General Catalyst. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface; product documentation and the application console sit behind authentication.

companies.name: Paradigm Health
companies.description: Paradigm Health is an AI-native clinical trial platform connecting biopharma sponsors with a research-ready provider network spanning roughly 2,100 care locations across the United States. Founded in 2021 and headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, the company operates infrastructure implemented at healthcare provider organizations to make clinical research part of routine care. Its Study Conduct platform captures data directly from electronic health records and other structured and unstructured sources, algorithmically evaluates FDA-defined data points in real time, and transmits the critical safety and efficacy signals needed for regulatory determinations to trial sponsors and the FDA. Paradigm serves both trial sponsors (protocol optimization, feasibility and site selection, patient identification and enrollment, data collection and delivery, post-approval evidence) and research sites. The company acquired Flatiron Health's Clinical Research business, announced a research collaboration with the U.S. FDA, and is backed by ARCH Venture Partners, General Catalyst, and GV. Paradigm currently exposes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile captures its identity, legal, and published security/compliance surface.

companies.name: People Ai
companies.description: People.ai is an AI-powered revenue intelligence platform for sales leaders, RevOps, and CROs, now operating under the Backstory brand (people.ai redirects to backstory.ai). The platform automatically captures customer-facing activity (emails, meetings, calls, chats) from existing tools such as Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, Gmail, Outlook, Zoom, Teams, and Slack, then analyzes that activity against deal history to answer which deals are real, which are at risk, and what to do next. Core capabilities include deal-risk identification, pipeline visibility and touchpoint mapping, revenue forecasting validation, and automated CRM hygiene. People.ai is a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI surface; integrations are delivered as managed native connectors rather than a documented public API.

companies.name: People.ai
companies.description: People.ai is an AI-powered revenue intelligence platform for enterprise sales teams. It automatically captures sales activity and contact data from email, calendar, and meetings, matches it into CRM systems like Salesforce and Microsoft Dynamics 365, and delivers AI-driven forecasting, opportunity management, account execution, and engagement forensics to improve pipeline visibility and drive predictable revenue growth. People.ai integrates with Salesforce, Microsoft, Oracle, Slack, Zoom, Webex, 6sense, and ZoomInfo. It is delivered as an enterprise SaaS product and does not publish a public developer API; its trust and security posture is documented with SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27017, GDPR, and CSA STAR. As of 2026 People.ai has rebranded to Backstory (www.people.ai now 301-redirects to www.backstory.ai); the product login remains at app.people.ai.

companies.name: Revion
companies.description: Revion builds an AI-powered operating system for automotive retail service operations. Its voice-first platform lets dealership technicians dictate repair information hands-free, automatically structuring their speech into repair orders, multi-point inspections, and service recommendations in real time so shops can service more vehicles and capture more high-margin work. Revion is a Winter 2026 Y Combinator company based in New York City, operating across US and EU regions. As of this profile Revion is an early-stage product company with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this entry captures its public identity, security posture, and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Sage Care
companies.description: Sage Care (sagecare.ai) builds an AI-native, HIPAA-compliant software platform made exclusively for home care agencies. Its product bundles an AI receptionist, a purpose-built CRM, an AI notetaker and a clinical scribe that automate the intake, referral, scheduling and documentation work that home care operators handle every day. Sage Care integrates with existing home care management systems such as WellSky and AxisCare rather than replacing them, and ships native iOS and desktop applications for caregivers and office staff. The company is backed by General Catalyst and surfaced through its portfolio. As of this enrichment pass Sage Care publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation — it is an application vendor rather than an API provider, so this profile captures company identity and security/compliance posture only.

companies.name: Spheron
companies.description: Spheron Network is a decentralized GPU and cloud compute marketplace that aggregates enterprise-grade NVIDIA GPU capacity from certified Tier 3/4 data centers worldwide and exposes it through a single on-demand, per-minute billed interface. The marketplace covers H100, H200, B200, B300, A100, GH200, L40S, RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090, RTX 4090, and pre-order GB200/GB300/ R100 inventory, priced 40-60% below hyperscaler rates with spot, reserved, and custom-cluster (8-512+ GPU) options. Teams access the platform through a web dashboard, a documented REST API at app.spheron.ai/api, a TypeScript Protocol SDK, an MCP plugin for Claude, SkyPilot integration, and Helm charts for self-hosted provider nodes. The Spheron Foundation also maintains an open compute protocol with Fizz nodes, provider nodes, ICL YAML configuration, and an on-chain payment system supporting both traditional payment rails and USDC/USDT stablecoin settlement. The company is transitioning from a pure decentralized protocol model toward an enterprise GPU procurement and aggregation marketplace while keeping the underlying provider network open and community-operated.

companies.name: Sumary
companies.description: Sumary is a Denmark-based fintech building an AI-native workflow engine for finance and accounting teams. Its platform layers autonomous accounting agents, anomaly detection, and on-demand reporting over a company's existing accounting systems — automating reconciliations and variance explanations, validating transactions to catch errors and potential fraud, and generating management reports, margin analyses, and cost breakdowns for bookkeepers, controllers, CFOs, and finance leaders. The company raised a $4.2M (27M DKK) pre-seed round led by byFounders with participation from Partech and Tenity. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface has been located; this profile captures the company's web, trust, and domain-security surface.

companies.name: Symbl.ai
companies.description: Symbl.ai is a conversation-intelligence platform for understanding and generating insights from human conversations across voice, video, and text. Its developer platform exposed Async, Streaming, and Telephony APIs plus the Nebula LLM for real-time speech-to-text and conversational insights — action items, topics, questions, follow-ups, sentiment, and custom trackers — with first-party SDKs for JavaScript, Web (browser), Python, and Go. Symbl.ai was acquired by Invoca; the standalone developer platform (api./docs./platform. symbl.ai) has since been decommissioned, but the official client SDKs remain published on npm, PyPI, pkg.go.dev, and the github.com/symblai organization, and the marketing, blog, pricing, and support surfaces stay live.

companies.name: Traba
companies.description: Traba is a New York City-based staffing marketplace and AI operating layer for the industrial supply chain, founded in 2021 and backed by Founders Fund. Traba connects vetted, high-reliability light-industrial workers with production plants, warehouses, and distribution centers, and pairs that staffing marketplace with Neo, an AI intelligence layer that unifies live operational data across WMS, ERP, HRIS, TMS, and payroll systems, surfaces root causes, and automates approved supply chain workflows. Traba publishes no public developer API.

companies.name: Verdant
companies.description: Verdant is an AI-native land-use permitting and planning software platform for local governments, spanning the entire process from a resident's first question through plan review to a commission's final vote. Applicants file complete, compliant applications upfront, and Verdant's AI reads documents, site plans, and diagrams to flag issues and draft staff review reports that municipal staff can approve. The platform is modular, letting jurisdictions buy only the modules they need, configured to their ordinances, workflows, and forms, and includes ordinance-research tooling to benchmark against peer jurisdictions and find gaps in local codes. Verdant is a Y Combinator Summer 2026 company; it currently ships an application product for cities and does not publish a public developer API.

companies.name: Asepha
companies.description: Asepha is an AI workflow automation platform built specifically for pharmacies, positioning itself as "the context graph for the therapy-start journey" with a stated vision to make medication delays impossible. Its AI agents automate repetitive pharmacy operations across automated prescription data entry, back-office work, 340B management (TPA matching, accruals, purchase-order automation), medication reconciliation (Best Possible Medication History), a conversational voice call assistant, benefits verification and prior-authorization (BV/PA) automation, REMS compliance reporting, and medication therapy review. The company reports outcomes such as a 32% reduction in manual labour cost within one month and tasks completed 4x faster than baseline. Asepha is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and HIPAA compliant, with AES-256 encryption at rest. Founded by CEO Eunice Wu, PharmD and CTO Can Uncu, the company operates from New York, NY and Toronto, ON, and is a Techstars portfolio company. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Asepha publishes no public API, developer portal, or specifications at this time.

companies.name: Brand.ai
companies.description: Brand.ai (Access to Tools Inc.) is a San Francisco-based AI platform for brand management that converts a company's brand assets into machine-readable intelligence so that people and AI agents can maintain brand consistency across tools and workflows. The product has two parts: Brand OS, which structures brand data through a Brand Foundation, Brand Ontology, Daily Signals and connected applications; and Brand Studio, which provides asset creation, a visual strategy Canvas, project management and Brand Check validation. Founded in 2024 and backed by Uncork Capital, the company targets brand builders, agencies and enterprise teams. Brand.ai is not a public developer API provider — it is a demo-gated SaaS platform with a published security posture (SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, CCPA), a Vanta trust center and a public status page, but no public API, SDK or developer portal at this time.

companies.name: Courier Health
companies.description: Courier Health is the patient experience platform for life sciences and biopharma. It gives pharmaceutical patient services, market access, and field reimbursement teams a single command center to manage the patient journey from prescription through long-term treatment adherence, using AI-generated patient summaries, workflow automation and orchestration, and integration of data across systems and partners. The company reports gains in patient starts, six-month persistency, and team productivity, and delivers the product as a HIPAA-compliant, SOC 2 Type II SaaS platform. Courier Health is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. No public developer or API surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company identity and its published security/compliance posture.

companies.name: Govini
companies.description: Govini (rebranded to Air, air.ai, in 2026) is a defense-technology and decision-analytics company whose Ark platform combines proprietary defense acquisition data with AI-enabled applications to close the national-security "Readiness Gap" across supply chain, science and technology, production, sustainment, logistics, and modernization missions. Ark holds FedRAMP High authorization and a DISA Impact Level 5 (IL5) Provisional Authorization plus service-level IL5 ATOs, making it a closed, government-authorized SaaS platform rather than a public developer API. Led by CEO Tara Murphy Dougherty and backed by investors including Accel and Bain Capital. This profile entered the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and has been enriched with the provider's real public identity, security posture, and published compliance authorizations.

companies.name: Joyful
companies.description: Joyful Health provides AI-assisted revenue recovery for healthcare organizations, combining automated claim investigation with expert billing teams to recover unpaid and denied insurance claims. Its platform runs inside an organization's existing revenue-cycle-management (RCM) systems rather than replacing them, covering denial investigation and root-cause analysis, claims recovery and appeals management, historical accounts-receivable (A/R) assessment, payer follow-up, documentation review, and financial insight to prevent future denials. The company operates a customer application at app.joyfulhealth.io and maintains a Vanta-hosted trust center. Joyful is a portfolio company of CRV. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; Joyful does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

companies.name: Qventus
companies.description: Qventus is a healthcare technology company that provides an AI-powered automation platform for hospital operations. Its "AI teammates" combine machine learning, generative AI, and behavioral science to streamline care-coordination workflows across surgical growth and operating-room utilization, perioperative and pre-admission-testing coordination, inpatient capacity and discharge planning, and care-gap and coding automation. Qventus sells to health systems and hospitals as a B2B SaaS product and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners, Mayfield, Norwest Venture Partners, and Y Combinator.

companies.name: DeepIP

Built on Docker Compose, with a thin CLI client talking to a local coastd daemon over a unix socket plus a bundled React/Vite web observability UI, Coasts is local-first and offline-capable, with optional extension to remote machines over SSH. Backed by Y Combinator (Fall 2025) and founded by Jamie Sunderland and Dan Hyman.

companies.name: Lithium Finance
companies.description: Lithium Finance is a decentralized asset-pricing protocol that combines machine learning with collective intelligence to value illiquid assets, with an initial focus on NFTs. Quantitative models analyze historical trading data to produce a base valuation and to flag cases where machine learning struggles — such as rare NFTs with little trading history — and the protocol then incentivizes a community of Price Experts to submit pricing estimates through on-chain Pricing Quests. Two ecosystem roles drive the network: Price Seekers (data consumers such as projects, lenders, issuers and analysts) fund prize pools to post asset-pricing enquiries, and Price Experts (brokers, traders and market participants) answer them for bounties. The economy runs on the LITH token plus non-transferable Reputation Points, and the protocol is governed by the Lithium DAO via Snapshot. The public surface is a set of Solidity Enquiry Pool, Reputation and LITH token contracts rather than a hosted web API.

companies.name: Matterworks
companies.description: Matterworks is a Boston-based life-sciences AI company building foundation models for biochemical omics. Its Large Spectral Model is trained on billions of small-molecule, lipid, peptide, and protein mass-spectrometry spectra across millions of biological contexts, and its Pyxis platform turns raw omics data into quantitative, untargeted biochemical annotations and predictions used for asset and target discovery, mode-of-action elucidation, and life-science R&D pipeline decisions. Matterworks positions biochemical omics as explaining orders of magnitude more biological variation than sequence data alone. The product is accessed through the Pyxis web application (app.matterworks.ai, Auth0 sign-in); no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface is published at this time.

companies.name: Mech-Mind Robotics
companies.description: Mech-Mind Robotics provides industrial 3D cameras (the Mech-Eye industrial 3D camera and laser profiler line) together with software suites — Mech-Vision machine-vision software, Mech-Viz robot-programming software, and the Mech-DLK deep-learning toolkit — that give industrial robots embodied AI and 3D vision. Typical applications include bin picking, depalletizing, machine tending, piece picking, and item picking; the company reports 3000+ deployed applications for 1000+ clients worldwide. The developer surface is the Mech-Eye SDK (a C++ core with Python and C# bindings), ROS and ROS2 interfaces, and the Mech-DLK SDK, all published under the MechMindRobotics GitHub organization; there is no public REST/HTTP API.

companies.name: Rebellions

The RBLN SDK compiles and serves HuggingFace Transformers/Diffusers, PyTorch, and TensorFlow models on RBLN accelerators, with integrations for vLLM, NVIDIA Triton, TorchServe, and Kubernetes. Rebellions does not expose a public REST/HTTP API; developers integrate through first-party Python SDKs (optimum-rbln, vllm-rbln), the RBLN compiler and driver, and the model zoo. Backed by Kindred Ventures and partnered with Samsung, Arm, IBM, and AWS.

companies.name: Spring Health
companies.description: Spring Health is a New York City-based digital mental health company that sells a comprehensive mental healthcare benefit to employers, health plans, brokers, channel partners, and healthcare providers. Its platform combines a clinically validated assessment, AI-driven matching, and a curated provider network to deliver therapy, medication management, coaching, an Employee Assistance Program (EAP), critical-incident response, work-life services, and self-guided digital exercises through a unified member experience branded Spring Life. For health plans and providers, Spring Health offers Springworks — its enterprise care-coordination and care-management offering — alongside a generative-AI member-facing assistant called Guide and clinician-facing AI tooling. Customers include General Mills, Hearst, and Moda Health, and the company publishes outcomes, research, and ROI evidence on long-term cost savings of mental health benefits. Spring Health operates as a B2B2C benefit: it does not expose a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documented HTTP API. Integrations with HRIS, SSO, eligibility files, and health-plan partners are delivered through enterprise implementation rather than a self-service API, and its GitHub organization (github.com/SpringHealth) has no public repositories.

companies.name: Ambiq Micro

This is not a web/REST API provider; it is profiled here for its open-source developer and AI SDK footprint.

companies.name: Descartes Labs
companies.description: Descartes Labs was a Santa Fe, New Mexico geospatial intelligence company founded in 2014 as a spin-out from Los Alamos National Laboratory. The company built the Descartes Labs Platform, a cloud-native geospatial data refinery and analytics environment combining a petabyte-scale satellite imagery archive (Landsat, Sentinel-1/2, MODIS, NAIP, PlanetScope, SkySat, commercial radar, NEXRAD weather radar, plus client-uploaded data) with a Python client library, JupyterHub-based workbench, and distributed compute for training and running deep learning and remote-sensing models at scale. Customers in agriculture, mining, energy, defense, insurance, and the U.S. government used the platform to build production geospatial machine learning pipelines covering crop forecasting, mineral exploration, infrastructure monitoring, methane detection, wildfire response, and ESG reporting. The Platform exposed a Catalog (imagery, bands, products, blobs, events), a Compute service (containerised functions, jobs, schedules), a Vector service (tabular and geospatial features), Dynamic Compute (lazy raster algebra and tiling), Auth, and a `descarteslabs` CLI. In October 2024, EarthDaily Analytics — backed by Antarctica Capital — acquired Descartes Labs and the Descartes Labs Government, Inc. subsidiary, folding the team, customers, and platform into the EarthDaily Constellation programme. The product was rebranded EarthOne in 2025; the `descarteslabs` Python package has been formally discontinued in favour of `earthdaily-earthone` (v5.x), the github.com/descarteslabs organisation has been renamed to `dlarchives`, www.descarteslabs.com is now a parked domain, and the docs.descarteslabs.com developer portal has been retired in favour of EarthDaily-hosted EarthOne documentation. This catalog entry preserves the historical Descartes Labs Platform surface as an archive — see the EarthDaily / EarthOne profile for the active product.

As of this enrichment pass Spike ships consumer and team applications but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; the profile below captures its real product, security posture, and public link surface.

companies.name: Turintech

Artemis spans AI inference, agentic software, latency-critical infrastructure, and planning & scheduling, and is driven through the Artemis CLI, which imports Git repositories, generates and validates AI-optimized code versions (via LLM, agent, or genetic-algorithm methods), runs compile/test/benchmark validation, and opens optimization pull requests. TurinTech also offers evoML for automated machine-learning model building. Access is via the Artemis CLI and platform using an API key (ARTEMIS_API_KEY). The company is backed by Speedinvest.

Deployments run in cloud, private VPC, or fully on-premises, are model-agnostic, and are governed with RBAC, SSO, lineage tracking, and audit logs. Founded by Shay Levi, Larissa Schneider, and Adi Azarya, with offices in Cupertino, Tel Aviv, and Berlin; backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and others; acquired Swish AI. Sales-led platform with no public developer API surface today.

Zama publishes the ERC-7984 confidential token standard, a developer hub, GitBook documentation, and an active open-source GitHub organization. Aventon operates no traditional public developer API of its own, but its Shopify-powered storefront at aventon.com natively exposes agent-facing commerce surfaces: a published /llms.txt, Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect discovery, and a live Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint for agent-driven catalog search, cart, and checkout.

The direct-to-consumer storefront at hawthorne.co runs on Shopify and exposes a modern agent-commerce surface: a published /llms.txt and /agents.md, Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect discovery, and a live Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint so AI shopping agents can search the catalog, build a cart, and complete a buyer-approved checkout.
