companies.name: Theta EdgeCloud
companies.description: Theta EdgeCloud is a distributed, hybrid AI and video cloud built on the Theta Network blockchain, offering on-demand GPU compute for AI model training, fine-tuning, inference, video transcoding, and live streaming. EdgeCloud aggregates GPU capacity from data-center hyperscaler partners and a global community of Edge Nodes (consumer and enterprise GPUs) into a single dispatchable compute layer addressable via REST, JSON-RPC, and SDK clients. Core services include EdgeCloud AI Services (on-demand model inference APIs for LLMs, image, audio, and multimodal models such as Llama, Stable Diffusion, FLUX, and Whisper; agentic RAG chatbots; GPU-backed Jupyter notebooks; dedicated GPU pod deployments; and AI training with GPU clusters), EdgeCloud Video Services (the Theta Video API for upload, transcoding, livestream ingestion, DRM, NFT-gated playback, and webhooks), EdgeStore (decentralized object storage), and the EdgeCloud Client (an installable node that earns TFUEL for contributing GPU and bandwidth). Developers authenticate with x-api-key tokens issued from the EdgeCloud dashboard, manage deployments programmatically through api.thetaedgecloud.com and the Node.js SDK @thetalabs/theta-edgecloud, and access on-demand model endpoints (also distributed through RapidAPI). The Theta blockchain layer is EVM-compatible with an Ethereum RPC adaptor, supports TNT-20 tokens and NFTs, and underwrites EdgeCloud's payment, rewards, and staking economy through the THETA governance token and TFUEL gas token. Theta operates as Theta Labs, headquartered in San Jose, California.

It connects any machine - Siemens, Allen-Bradley, Fanuc, KUKA, ABB, and legacy PLCs - through 135 native OT connectors, generates control logic from a natural-language description of a process (up to 15x faster than traditional PLC programming), and runs the full stack at the edge on purpose-built industrial controllers with no cloud required. The platform layers hardware, live data dashboards and SCADA views, interoperability, physical AI, and zero-trust OT/IT cybersecurity (NIS2 and NIST aligned) into one stack, with real-time browser-based monitoring across 800,000+ machine hours. Vitesse exposes a marketing website and a login-gated product application; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer documentation.

companies.description: Atlas is an AI implementation partner built for independent accounting firms, deploying supervised, firm-specific AI "junior accountants" that automate repetitive, data-intensive workflows such as client onboarding, follow-ups, bookkeeping, compliance, and financial reporting while keeping human accountants in control of every decision and client relationship. Founded by Arpit Maheshwari (CEO) and Jagmal Singh (CTO) and co-led by Accel and Stellaris with Felicis participation, Atlas raised a $6M seed round in 2026 to scale its network of partner firms across North America. Atlas is currently a services-led AI company and publishes no public API, SDKs, or developer portal.

companies.name: Birdstop
companies.description: Birdstop is an American autonomous-drone and remote-sensing company that lets organizations monitor and inspect field assets at scale without personnel onsite. Its Fealty system is an all-weather, always-on drone that launches in under three seconds, flies for up to 45 minutes, cruises at 45 mph, and patrols 24/7 across public safety, utilities, transportation, construction, and data-center sites. Birdstop pairs networked UAVs and ground stations with computer vision and a patented optical/acoustic detect-and-avoid system to enable safe beyond-visual-line-of-sight flight under some of the FAA's most advanced approvals, delivering Observation-on-Demand intel over the internet. The company is FAA-authorized, SOC 2 certified, and NDAA compliant, and builds its drones in Detroit. Backed by Techstars, Birdstop currently exposes no public developer API; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Blue River Technology
companies.description: Blue River Technology is an agricultural robotics and machine-learning company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, and a wholly owned subsidiary of John Deere (Deere & Company), which acquired it in 2017. Founded in 2011 by Jorge Heraud and Lee Redden out of Stanford University, the company builds intelligent machinery that combines computer vision, machine learning, robotics, and full-stack software to make farming more precise and sustainable. Its flagship product, See & Spray, uses onboard cameras and deep-learning models to distinguish crops from weeds in real time and target herbicide only where it is needed, dramatically reducing chemical use. Blue River operates as John Deere's autonomy and computer-vision engineering hub, applying the same perception and edge-AI stack across agriculture, construction, and mining equipment. The company does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; its technology ships embedded in John Deere machinery and is surfaced to growers through John Deere Operations Center rather than a standalone developer program.

companies.name: Buildots
companies.description: Buildots is an AI-powered construction intelligence platform headquartered in Tel Aviv, Israel, with offices in London and the United States. The company combines 360-degree hardhat-mounted cameras with computer vision and machine learning models that automatically capture, locate, and classify on-site construction progress against the project BIM model and schedule, producing trade-level performance data, deviation and delay detection, and portfolio-wide analytics for general contractors, project teams, executives, and owners. Buildots reports that projects using the platform together with a performance-driven operating approach have reduced delays by up to 50%. The product family includes Buildots (the AI construction intelligence platform), Genda (workforce intelligence), and a fully managed Capture Services operation that handles routine site capture for customers. Verticals served include data centers, commercial, multifamily, healthcare, industrial, education, and airports. Notable customers shown on the website include Intel, Mortenson, JE Dunn, Turner, Wates, and STO. Buildots was founded in 2018 and is led by CEO and co-founder Roy Danon with co-founders Aviv Leibovici (CPO) and Yakir Sudry (CCO). Investors include Lightspeed Venture Partners, Future Energy Ventures, Viola Ventures, TLV Partners, OG Ventures, and Tencent. Buildots does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; integrations with construction software (e.g., Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud) are arranged directly through the company.

companies.name: CODEX.md
companies.description: CODEX.md is a project-level Markdown memory file that the OpenAI Codex CLI loads to bootstrap an AI coding agent with persistent project instructions, coding conventions, build and test commands, and team conventions. The OpenAI Codex CLI now standardizes on AGENTS.md as the canonical filename, with CODEX.md and codex.md historically used and still recognized as fallback configuration filenames. Files are discovered through a three-tier hierarchy spanning the user's home directory, the Git repository root, and the current working directory, with closer files overriding earlier guidance when concatenated into the model prompt.

companies.name: GEMINI.md
companies.description: GEMINI.md is the project context file convention used by the Google Gemini CLI to provide project-specific instructions, coding standards, architectural notes, and development workflows to the Gemini AI agent. The format follows a hierarchical, plain Markdown structure that the Gemini CLI loads automatically from the working directory and parent directories, layering global, project, and subproject context. It mirrors similar agent context conventions like CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md.

companies.name: Habana Labs
companies.description: Habana Labs is an artificial-intelligence processor company, now part of Intel, that designs deep-learning accelerators for AI training and inference. Its Gaudi (training) and Goya (inference) processors — sold today as the Intel Gaudi 2 and Gaudi 3 AI accelerators — are programmed through the SynapseAI software suite, which integrates with PyTorch and DeepSpeed and ships reference models, containers, and installation tooling. Habana was founded in 2016 in Israel and acquired by Intel in 2019. Its public developer surface is not a hosted web API but an open-source SDK and toolchain: the HabanaAI GitHub organization (reference models, PyTorch bridge, setup/install, plus vLLM and Megatron forks) and the Intel Gaudi documentation at docs.habana.ai. This profile catalogs that developer footprint for the API Evangelist network.

companies.description: Sainapse, built by Bayestree Intelligence, is a unified, explainable AI engine for customer support, outreach, and operations that is embedded directly in an enterprise's environment. It connects to existing integrations to source real-time data for autonomous resolution, grounds every response in verified sources of data, and can act as an agent copilot (next best actions, suggested responses) or as an autonomous agent. Sainapse learns from human-in-the-loop corrections and evolving business rules, supports 220+ integrations, and is offered as a hosted service or deployed on-premises. It publishes SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, and GDPR compliance. Sainapse is an enterprise, demo-led product with no public self-serve API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification at this time.

Its platform spans four core products: the Notified Body Suite (intake-to-certificate workflow management), Scheduling Agents (automated auditor assignment and travel optimization), Tech File Review (structured technical-documentation assessment against regulatory requirements), and Report Writing (AI-assisted drafting of compliance reports). Seamflow is an early-stage enterprise-SaaS company ($4.5M seed) backed by Initialized Capital and Northzone. As of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI specification; this record captures its verified public company surface.

companies.name: Spiral
companies.description: Spiral (SpiralDB) is a multimodal data platform built for the "machine consumer" — frontier AI systems and agents. It unifies video, images, audio, embeddings, point clouds, sensor streams, tables, and text under one query language and coordinate-frame system, serving everything from raw bytes to model-ready tensors at machine-scale throughput for pretraining pipelines and agentic access. Spiral is the creator of Vortex, a high-performance extensible columnar data format (100x faster random access and 10-20x faster scans vs. Apache Parquet) now incubating under the Linux Foundation, along with the FastLanes, FSST, and ALP compression libraries. The hosted Spiral warehouse is currently invite-only (Request Access); the public developer surface today is the open-source Vortex ecosystem (Python and Rust bindings). Backed by Amplify Partners and General Catalyst.

Clients hand off a sourcing need and Andustry returns a verified supplier shortlist within 24-48 hours, delivering an average of roughly 30% cost savings and 2x faster sourcing timelines on a commission-only basis with no subscription. This profile was surfaced via the a16z network (through founder Ronny Conway's a16z tenure) and enriched from the firm's public website. A.Capital is a venture capital firm and does not publish a developer-facing API surface, developer portal, or API artifacts.

companies.description: Archimetis builds an AI-powered Operational Reasoning System for refineries, chemicals, and heavy process industries. Marketed as "See more. Solve smarter," it targets margin improvement, cost savings, and process safety across refining, chemicals, and other heavy industries. The platform supports industrial robotic arms, humanoid robots, and custom systems, and targets use cases such as data collection for Physical AI training, remote real-world robot deployment, and supervised autonomy with human oversight. Integration is handled during onboarding by sharing a robot's URDF and joint control API rather than through a public developer API. As an early-stage startup, Avea Robotics publishes a website, Notion-hosted documentation, and a Substack blog, but does not yet expose a public REST API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a self-serve developer platform.

companies.name: Incandor
companies.description: Incandor is a San Francisco based Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building behavioral intelligence infrastructure for fraud and abuse detection. Rather than relying on identity verification at account creation, Incandor constructs a behavioral map of every user on a platform from how they physically interact with an app or website — mouse dynamics, keystroke timing, scroll patterns, and on mobile how a device is held. It requires no fraud labels and no enrollment period, working from the first session. At the individual level it identifies account takeovers with greater than 99 percent accuracy; at the population level it separates out coordinated fraud rings, mule operators, shared operators, bots and agents, and coerced or duress sessions. Incandor is delivered as a programmable API and a client-side telemetry SDK rather than a black-box risk score, letting fraud teams combine behavioral signals with their own transaction history, customer records, and business rules. It collects only behavioral signals — not what users type, read, or view — keeping user data private by design. The company was founded by Matthew Yekell (CEO) and Luc Rosenzweig (CTO), both Stanford CS graduates. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; the developer platform is currently early access.

The result is a small-footprint, private-by-design engine that runs fully on-device, is robust to noise, and works across languages and accents. Fluent.ai licenses two core products to OEMs and ODMs: Fluent.ai Air (Automatic Intent Recognition), an on-device command-recognition engine, and Fluent.ai Wakeword, a small-footprint wake-word / keyword-spotting solution. Fraudio integrates with customers through a plug-and-play real-time scoring API with sub-100ms response times, configurable risk-appetite thresholds, and no upfront integration or setup cost. Customers include Viva Wallet, Silverflow, Pismo, Bancontact, Fazz, PayTabs, IXOPAY, Bold.co, SaltPay, WiPay, ePayco, and LOQR. Fraudio is ISO 27001 certified, was selected for the Visa Innovation Program (2023), is co-financed by the EU Lisboa 2030 programme, has raised roughly $3.3M seed plus a Series A round (March 2025), and counts BigStar Ventures, BYND Venture Capital, Teya, Viva Wallet, Portugal Ventures, Iberis Capital, Shilling, and CTT among its investors. Its FruitScope platform mounts AI-enabled cameras on any farm vehicle to collect precise per-tree and per-vine data — fruit count, size, color, and growth rate — which is stored in FruitScope Vault and surfaced through FruitScope OS for crop decision-making, with a Vineyard Robotics division serving grape growers. Backed by General Catalyst, the company has raised roughly $22M. As of this profile Orchard Robotics publishes a marketing and careers website but no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

companies.name: PeopleFund, Perfect Technologies
companies.description: PFC Technologies (formerly PeopleFund) is a Seoul, South Korea fintech company operating at the intersection of direct online lending and AI lending infrastructure. It runs two platforms: CPLE (Crople), an online investment-linked finance (온라인투자연계금융) service that matches retail investors with consumer and small-business loans, and AIRPACK, an AI-powered, no-code underwriting and loan operations infrastructure (AIRPACK-Lab for data analysis, model development and approval-rule tuning, and AIRPACK-Studio for model deployment, rule-set operation and performance monitoring) sold to savings banks and other lending institutions. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI, SDK, or partner API surface; AIRPACK integrations are handled through a direct sales/contact process. This record was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched as an API Evangelist network company profile.

Presto offers a full spectrum of operating modes (supervised AI, pure AI, agent-led, and unsupervised AI) and has expanded into AI-native phone ordering for QSRs. Presto Voice integrates into existing drive-thru hardware, confirmation boards, headsets, and POS platforms through partnerships with vendors such as Oracle, PAR, and Qu, and draws on AI partnerships with OpenAI and ElevenLabs. Presto does not publish a public or partner-facing developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; integrations are arranged directly with the company through vendor and POS partnerships, so no API products are listed here.

companies.name: Tractable
companies.description: Tractable is a London-headquartered artificial intelligence company founded in 2014 by Alexandre Dalyac, Razvan Ranca, and Adrien Cohen that applies computer vision and deep learning to automate visual damage assessment for auto and property insurance claims. The platform analyzes photos of vehicles and buildings down to the pixel to produce accident first-notice- of-loss (FNOL) triage decisions, AI-generated preliminary repair estimates, automated claim review for fraud and consistency, subrogation packet analysis, and property repair-cost estimation and underwriting condition assessment. Tractable's flagship offerings include Auto Estimator, Auto Damage Appraiser, Auto Salvage, Property Estimator, Property Underwriter, and the LumaScanner fixed-operations vehicle scanning product. The company serves insurers, dealerships, repair networks, recyclers, and fleet and rental operators including GEICO, Aviva, Mitchell, Tokio Marine, Admiral, Sompo, Aioi Nissay Dowa, and LKQ. Tractable reached unicorn status in June 2021 and secured a $65M investment from SoftBank Vision Fund 2 in July 2023, scaling to over 300 employees across offices in London, Warsaw, Paris, Milan, Spain, Romania, New York, Toronto, Tokyo, and Bangkok. The product is delivered through flexible desktop and API integrations with FNOL, estimatics, and claim review systems, but the developer surface is gated to enterprise partners — there is no public developer portal, self-service API key, OpenAPI specification, SDK release, or open-source repository, and no publicly published authentication, endpoint, pricing, or rate-limit documentation.

companies.name: Arc Institute
companies.description: Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit biomedical research organization headquartered in Palo Alto, California, co-founded in 2021 by Silvana Konermann (Executive Director), Patrick Hsu (Core Investigator), and Stripe co-founder Patrick Collison. With 300+ staff ("Arconauts") across 9 core laboratories and 5 technology centers, Arc develops AI foundation models for biology that span DNA, RNA, proteins, and single cells. Its flagship releases include Evo (Science, 2024) and Evo 2 (Nature, 2026) — DNA foundation models trained on trillions of nucleotides at single-nucleotide resolution with up to a 1-megabase context; STATE and Stack single-cell foundation models for cellular perturbation and in-context learning; the Arc Virtual Cell Atlas; the SRAgent LLM agents for bioinformatics; and the BINSEQ binary sequencing format. Models are released under Apache 2.0 on GitHub and Hugging Face, with hosted inference for Evo 2 available through NVIDIA BioNeMo and the NVIDIA build.nvidia.com API. Arc is funded by philanthropic donations from Patrick and John Collison, Vitalik Buterin, the Ron Conway family, Dustin Moskovitz, Daniel Gross, Elad Gil, and other technology benefactors; it does not sell APIs, SaaS, or models commercially.

companies.name: Caper
companies.description: Caper (caper.ai) is a New York-founded computer-vision company that builds AI-powered smart shopping carts and cashierless checkout technology for grocery and retail. Its Caper Cart uses a set of onboard cameras and deep-learning object recognition, running on NVIDIA Jetson edge AI, to auto-detect items as shoppers add them and let customers skip the checkout line. Founded in 2016 (Y Combinator) by Lindon Gao and team, Caper was acquired by Instacart in 2021 for roughly $350M and now operates as part of the Instacart Enterprise Platform (Connected Stores), deployed with retailers including ALDI and Coles. Caper ships retail hardware and an internal edge/vision platform; it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or a developer portal.

companies.name: Collegevine
companies.description: CollegeVine is a Cambridge, Massachusetts company, backed by Menlo Ventures, that has repositioned itself as "the AI operating system for universities." Its platform pairs automated ingestion of data from campus systems (a Data layer) with a unified Ontology of institutional operations and an AI Operations layer of agents, applications, and ML models that connect directly to a university's CRM and admissions workflows. CollegeVine also operates a large consumer-facing college-admissions guidance property (chancing engine, essay guidance, and an AI counselor) at collegevine.com and blog.collegevine.com. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, developer portal, or published SDK for its product; engagement is enterprise sales and demo driven. It does maintain an active public GitHub organization of open-source PureScript, Haskell, and TypeScript libraries.

companies.name: Confluence Labs
companies.description: Confluence Labs is a San Francisco AI research company (Y Combinator Winter 2026, backed by Paul Graham) focused on learning efficiency — building machine learning systems that learn from limited data and few experiments. Founded by Brent Burdick and Niranjan Baskaran, the lab works on hypothesis generation (using AI to design maximally informative experiments) and data-efficient modeling (combining large language models with discrete program search) to accelerate breakthroughs in data-sparse domains such as drug design, materials engineering, hardware, and physics discovery. The team reported state-of-the-art performance on the ARC-AGI-2 reasoning benchmark using LLM-driven program synthesis and open-sourced their solver on GitHub. Confluence Labs currently publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface; this profile captures verified company identity for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Hawk-Eye Innovations
companies.description: Hawk-Eye Innovations is a Basingstoke, UK-headquartered sports technology company and part of the Sony Group, specializing in precision optical tracking, electronic officiating, video replay, and performance analytics across 25+ professional sports in 100+ countries. Founded in 2001 by Paul Hawkins and acquired by Sony in 2011, Hawk-Eye operates alongside Pulselive and Beyond Sports within Sony's sports division. The company is the standard for ball-tracking in tennis (Electronic Line Calling, now used in place of human line judges at the major tours), goal-line technology and semi-automated offside in football (Premier League, FIFA), video replay in cricket (DRS), NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, rugby, and PGA Tour shot-tracking. Core product platforms include SMART Replay, SMART Track, SMART Insight, HawkAR, iHawk, HawkREPLAY, HawkNEST, HawkVISION, SkeleTRACK, Electronic Line Calling, Goal Line Technology, Semi-Automated Offside Technology, and VAR systems. Revenue comes from long-term contracts with leagues, federations, and broadcasters; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Hawk-Eye products. All integrations are bespoke and delivered through Sony Sports Business / Hawk-Eye operations teams.

companies.name: HiddenLayer
companies.description: HiddenLayer is an Austin, Texas-based AI security company founded in March 2022 by Chris Sestito (CEO), Tanner Burns (Chief Scientist), and Jim Ballard (CIO) — former Cylance researchers who encountered a real-world attack on production ML models. HiddenLayer builds an AI Security Platform that protects machine learning and generative AI systems across their entire lifecycle, comprising four integrated modules: AI Discovery (catalogs AI assets and eliminates shadow AI), AI Supply Chain Security (Model Scanner inspects models, weights, and pickle/RDS files for malicious payloads and backdoors), AI Attack Simulation (continuous adversarial red-teaming for agentic and generative systems), and AI Runtime Security / AIDR (a real-time detection-and-response firewall using deterministic classifiers that sit outside the model inference path to detect prompt injection, jailbreaks, indirect attacks, data leakage, and malicious tool calls in agentic and MCP systems). The platform exposes native connectors for CI/CD, MLOps, SIEM/SOAR, API gateways, and major data and cloud platforms, plus guardrail integrations for OpenAI Agents, LangChain, AWS Strands, Microsoft Agent Framework, Azure APIM, and a GitHub Action for Model Scanner. HiddenLayer publishes Python, TypeScript, and Java/Kotlin SDKs and research-grade tooling such as HiddenPickle (Python pickle disassembler/patcher) and HiddenPromise (R .rdx/.rdb/.rds disassembler). The company has raised $56M total ($50M Series A in September 2023 led by M12 / Microsoft's Venture Fund and Moore Strategic Ventures, with Booz Allen Ventures, IBM Ventures, Capital One Ventures, and Ten Eleven Ventures participating) and serves Fortune 500 enterprises, financial services, and US Federal agencies. The HiddenLayer SaaS console and REST API are gated behind enterprise sales and not publicly self-serve, placing this profile in Tier-3 (enterprise-gated) coverage.

companies.name: Humans
companies.description: humans& is a human-centric frontier AI lab founded in 2025 and publicly announced on January 20, 2026, building large-scale AI models centered on people and their relationships rather than raw autonomy. Its research spans long-horizon and multi-agent reinforcement learning, memory, and user understanding, tightly integrating science and product so that AI acts as connective tissue that strengthens organizations and communities. The founding team comes from frontier industry and academic labs including xAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Meta, Reflection, AI2, Stanford, and MIT. Its seed round is led by SV Angel and co-founder Georges Harik, with investors including NVIDIA, GV (Google Ventures), Emerson Collective, Forerunner, S32, DCVC, and Jeff Bezos. As a pre-product research lab it publishes no public API yet; this profile captures its verified public identity surfaces.

companies.name: Imbue
companies.description: Imbue is a San Francisco AI research lab building agentic foundation models for reasoning and the human tooling around them, with a stated mission of AI that is loyal to its user. The team trains large reasoning models in-house (including a 70B model trained from scratch with open-sourced tooling and evaluation datasets) and publishes research on agent and reasoning architectures, reinforcement learning, data generation, and the scientific theory of deep learning. Imbue ships practical tools that emerge from the research, including Sculptor and mngr for orchestrating parallel coding agents, Bouncer for filtering social feeds, and Blueprint and Vet. There is no public commercial inference API; integration happens through open-sourced repositories, model artifacts on Hugging Face, and research releases.

companies.name: Insilico Medicine
companies.description: Insilico Medicine is a clinical-stage biotechnology company applying generative AI and robotic automation to drug discovery and development. Its Pharma.AI software suite includes PandaOmics (target discovery from multi-omics data), Chemistry42 (generative chemistry with retrosynthesis, property prediction, and ADMET), Generative Biologics, inClinico (clinical trial outcome prediction), Science42 DORA (research assistant), Nach01, and PreciousGPT-family models for life sciences. The company runs its own therapeutic pipeline spanning oncology, fibrosis, and inflammation, with programs targeting TNIK, USP1, QPCTL, PHD, MAT2A, TEAD, ENPP1, KAT6 and others through Phase II. Insilico monetizes through Pharma.AI software licensing, partnerships with major pharmaceutical companies, and progression of its in-house assets. Pharma.AI tools are commercial SaaS products accessed via web UI; the company publishes open-source research code on GitHub (GENTRL, fcd_torch, BiAAE, DD-VAE, DORA) but does not expose a public commercial API.

companies.name: Magic

Its GitHub organization (magicproduct) hosts research tooling (e.g. hash-hop, a long-context evaluation harness) and infrastructure forks, not an API client or SDK.

companies.name: Muro AI
companies.description: Muro AI is an early-stage construction-technology startup building PrecOS, a pre-construction operating system marketed as a pre-con manager's AI assistant that carries general contractors from scoping through handover. The platform applies domain-adapted large language models, image models, agentic workflows, RAG pipelines, and document/plan parsing (OCR and computer vision) to automate bid comparison, estimation, bill-of-materials, and budget updates for teams that still run on spreadsheets. Muro is backed by Techstars and integrates with industry tools such as Procore. As of this profiling the company publishes a marketing site, a blog, and careers pages, but exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation, so this record captures identity and a domain-security probe rather than an API surface.

companies.name: Operand
companies.description: Operand is an AI-enabled pricing and commercial strategy platform for consumer retail, founded in 2024 and backed by Felicis, Y Combinator, SV Angel, and Soma Capital. It applies proprietary AI systems — an autonomous "agent swarm" — to set pricing and promotion strategy for mid-market and enterprise brands and retailers managing thousands of SKUs, volatile demand, and thin margins, running simulations to benchmark margin, revenue, and inventory-turn objectives before automating price changes. Operand is delivered as a managed platform with expert support and request-a-quote pricing rather than a public developer API; it currently publishes no OpenAPI, developer portal, or self-serve SDKs. An earlier Operand product at operand.ai offered an embeddings / semantic-search API with Python, Go, and TypeScript SDKs, now discontinued.

companies.name: Pachama
companies.description: Pachama is a San Francisco–based climate technology company founded in 2018 that built a satellite- and machine-learning-powered platform for monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) of nature-based carbon projects — including forest conservation, reforestation, afforestation, and improved forest management. Pachama combined satellite imagery, LiDAR, remote sensing, and deep-learning models to measure aboveground biomass, detect deforestation, and track project performance against verified baselines, surfacing that intelligence through an online marketplace where corporate buyers (including Microsoft, Shopify, Salesforce, Flexport.org, Mercado Libre, Boom Supersonic, and Nespresso) could discover and purchase high-integrity carbon credits. In November 2025, Pachama was acquired by Carbon Direct, and its proprietary digital MRV platform and forest-carbon science team were folded into Carbon Direct's science-backed carbon management offering; pachama.com now redirects to carbon-direct.com. Throughout its life as an independent company Pachama operated a buyer marketplace and discussed plans for a partner API to embed project selection and retirement data into third-party products, but never shipped a public, self-service developer API, SDK, or open OpenAPI specification — its GitHub organization contains only forks and archived internal tooling.

companies.name: Physical Intelligence
companies.description: Physical Intelligence (often styled "Pi" or "π") is a San Francisco-based research company building general-purpose foundation models for robotics with the stated goal of producing learning algorithms that can control any robot to do any task. The company has published a continuing line of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models: π0 (October 2024, first generalist multi-task multi-robot policy), π0-FAST (autoregressive variant via Real-time Action Chunking / FAST tokenization), π0.5 (April 2025, open-world generalization), π*0.6 (November 2025, reinforcement-learning from experience), and π0.7 (April 2026, steerable model with emergent capabilities). Physical Intelligence releases significant work as open source: the openpi repository (~12K stars) is the canonical home for π0 weights and code, with companion repos including real-time-chunking-kinetix, pi-data-sharing, aloha, augmax, and rlds_dataset_builder. The company does not yet offer a hosted commercial API; access to the platform is via open-weight models and research collaborations.

companies.name: Recursion Pharmaceuticals
companies.description: Recursion Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: RXRX) is a Salt Lake City-based AI-enabled drug discovery company that operates the Recursion Operating System (Recursion OS), a vertically integrated platform combining automated wet-lab cellular phenomics, transcriptomics (Trekseq), proteomics, ADME, chemistry, and patient data with machine learning to map biology and design drug candidates. The platform runs on BioHive-2, a NVIDIA-built supercomputer ranked among the top global systems and dedicated to biopharma workloads, and is fed by 50+ petabytes of proprietary biological and chemical data. In November 2024 Recursion completed the acquisition of Exscientia, folding Exscientia's generative AI chemistry, Centaur Chemist, and clinical pipeline into the combined company; Recursion now runs more than 10 clinical and preclinical programs (REC-4881 for FAP, REC-3565 MALT1 inhibitor, REC-1245 RBM39 for biomarker-enriched solid tumors and lymphomas, REC-617 CDK7 inhibitor, REC-994 for cerebral cavernous malformation, REC-2282 for NF2- mutated meningiomas, REC-4209 for IPF, REC-7735 for HSD obesity), 10+ advanced discovery programs, and 10+ partnered programs across Roche (Genentech), Bayer, Sanofi, and Merck KGaA (Darmstadt). Recursion does not currently expose paid commercial APIs to external developers; assets and data access are delivered through licensing, scientific collaborations, and the MapApp web product. Externally, Recursion ships substantial open tooling: the RxRx family of open phenomics datasets (RxRx1, RxRx2, RxRx3, RxRx3-core, RxRx19a, RxRx19b) hosted at rxrx.ai and Hugging Face, the OpenPhenom-S/16 foundation model (released on Hugging Face and Google Cloud's Model Garden, with Phenom-Beta on NVIDIA BioNeMo), the MolE molecular foundation model, the gflownet library for graph and molecular generative modeling, SynFlowNet/synflownet-boltz for retrosynthesis-aware molecular design, maes_microscopy (NeurIPS 2023 spotlight masked autoencoders for cell microscopy), and rxrx1-utils for the NeurIPS 2019 CellSignal competition. The combination positions Recursion as a Tier-2 AI drug discovery provider with no commercial API surface but a meaningful open-source and open-model presence aimed at the computational biology research community.

companies.name: Sportlogiq
companies.description: Sportlogiq is a Montreal, Quebec-based sports analytics company that applies patented computer vision and machine learning to broadcast video to generate high-resolution player tracking, event, and performance datasets across ice hockey, soccer/global football, American football, and youth sports. Founded in 2015 by Olympic figure skater Craig Buntin and computer-vision PhD Mehrsan Javan, the company is led by CEO Mitchell Wasserman and employs roughly 75 people, including a research team of ~13 AI scientists with 180+ patents and publications. Sportlogiq describes itself as the global leader in hockey analytics, with adoption across the majority of NHL franchises, 150+ professional and amateur hockey clubs worldwide, international hockey federations and leagues (SHL, PWHL, IIHF), NCAA hockey programs, NFL franchises, and global football organizations — collectively serving 220+ clients. In November 2024 Sportlogiq acquired 8BY8, a sports video infrastructure platform that combines multi-angle video, data streams, and audio for officiating, coaching, and player health workflows. In January 2026 Sportlogiq was itself acquired by Teamworks, where it continues to operate as the AI analytics layer of Teamworks' broader operating system for sport. Sportlogiq exposes its tracking and event data to teams, leagues, broadcasters, and analytics partners through a private partner API and bulk data feeds; there is no public developer portal, no self-service signup, no published OpenAPI specification, and no public SDKs or open-source repositories. Access is sold as part of commercial contracts and integrated directly into partner workflows.

companies.name: Celltype
companies.description: CellType is an AI-driven drug discovery company building what it calls "The Biological World Model" — foundation models and autonomous agents that simulate human biology to predict drug responses in human systems before clinical trials, reducing reliance on traditional preclinical models such as mice and cell lines. Its core technology, Cell2Sentence (C2S), teaches large language models to understand cellular biology by converting single-cell gene expression data into a text-like format that models can interpret, and the company reports using it to discover and validate a novel cancer treatment signal targeting tumor immunogenicity. A Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company based in New York City, CellType works with large pharmaceutical partners and currently operates as a B2B research and drug-discovery platform rather than a public developer API.

companies.name: GodHands
companies.description: GodHands is a Y Combinator-backed startup (2026, San Francisco) building deterministic computer-use infrastructure for AI agents. It provides a high-fidelity execution layer that acts as a translation interface between any model or agent runtime and the operating system, letting agents reliably operate across desktop and browser applications - including legacy software and API-less systems, on the premise that "if a human can see it, GodHands can interact with it." Instead of fragile, probabilistic vision-based UI automation, every action is designed to be repeatable and predictable, removing hallucination risk from the execution layer, and every action is captured in comprehensive, immutable audit logs for debugging, accountability, and regulatory compliance. The platform is organized around a Control Plane plus Iceberg and Vector surfaces, and is built as the execution engine for any LLM or agent framework. Positioned for regulated teams, claims-approval workflows, and moving records from legacy terminals into browser-based systems.

Its flagship model, ORION, converts Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data into high-resolution, photorealistic optical imagery in real time using deterministic one-step diffusion, overcoming the limitation that traditional optical satellites are unusable roughly 70% of the time due to weather and night cycles. The technology targets 24/7 situational awareness for defense and intelligence, commodities and financial analytics, disaster response, agriculture, and climate monitoring. companies.name: Bidgely
companies.description: Bidgely is a Mountain View, California energy analytics company that builds AI software for electric and gas utilities. Its flagship platform, UtilityAI, applies patented non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) and disaggregation techniques to smart meter interval data to infer appliance-level energy usage — air conditioning, heat pumps, electric vehicles, pool pumps, water heaters and more — from the whole-home meter signal alone, without surveys, sub-meters, or smart plugs. The platform layers GenAI natural-language interfaces and Agentic AI workflows on top of disaggregation to support utility programs across demand-side management, customer engagement and high-bill alerts, load flexibility and time-of-use, electrification (EV and heat pump targeting), grid resiliency and DER planning, affordability and income-qualified outreach, gas efficiency, small and mid-sized business programs, and energy theft detection. Bidgely is sold to utilities as SaaS or deployable into customer AWS, Snowflake, Databricks, Azure, and Oracle environments, and exposes embeddable customer-facing widgets to utility digital channels. Bidgely has been deployed by more than 50 utilities across four continents — including FortisBC, Arizona Public Service, PacifiCorp, Avista, NV Energy, Nova Scotia Power, and SoCalGas — covering tens of millions of meters. Bidgely operates an internal REST API surface across regional endpoints (naapi.bidgely.com, api.eu.bidgely.com) for its own pilot deployments and embeddable widgets, but does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or self-service API key program; integration is conducted under utility contracts.

Its platform combined generative chemistry (Centaur Chemist) with patient tissue-based screening (EVE, an automated single-cell platform for testing drug candidates directly against patient-derived tumor samples) to design small-molecule drug candidates faster and at lower cost than conventional pharma R&D. Notable firsts included EXS-21546 (an A2A antagonist developed with Evotec), DSP-1181 (the first AI-designed molecule to enter human clinical trials, with Sumitomo Dainippon Pharma), and DSP-0038 (a dual 5-HT1A/5-HT2A modulator for Alzheimer's psychosis). Exscientia maintained active pharma partnerships with Sanofi, Bristol Myers Squibb, Bayer, Sumitomo, and Merck KGaA. Exscientia was acquired by Recursion Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: RXRX) in an all-stock deal that closed in November 2024; the combined company operates under the Recursion brand and the legacy exscientia.ai website now redirects to recursion.com. The Exscientia name persists primarily through its GitHub organization, which continues to host open-source scientific Python packages for molecular predictive modelling (molflux), physics-based ML potentials (physicsml), antibody structure prediction (abodybuilder3), and biomolecular simulation (biosimspace) used by the wider computational chemistry and structural biology community. Exscientia did not expose any public commercial APIs, SDKs, or developer products before or after the merger; platform access was always delivered through collaborative drug-discovery agreements.

companies.name: Kuva Space
companies.description: Kuva Space is a Finnish space-data company headquartered in Espoo that operates a fleet of hyperspectral Earth observation microsatellites and delivers AI-driven planetary intelligence through its Kuva Sense platform. Founded in 2016 (originally as Reaktor Space Lab) by Tuomas Tikka and Janne Kuhno in collaboration with Reaktor, the company designs, builds, and operates its own 6U CubeSat-class spacecraft carrying a patented in-orbit tunable Fabry-Perot 2D snapshot hyperspectral imager. Its operational Hyperfield-1A (launched August 2024 on SpaceX Falcon 9 from Vandenberg) and Hyperfield-1B (launched June 2025) cover the 475–950 nm VNIR range with up to 160 tunable spectral bands at 25 m spatial resolution and a 50 km swath from a 500 km polar sun-synchronous orbit. The larger 70 kg Hyperfield-2 microsatellite, scheduled for H2 2026, expands coverage to 450–1,650 nm at 15 m resolution with an additional 3.6 m GSD RGB camera. By 2030 Kuva Space plans to grow the constellation to roughly 100 satellites to enable sub-daily revisit anywhere on Earth. Onboard AI handles cloud filtering, spectral band alignment, and compression so that downlinked products feed directly into Kuva Sense, where automated analytics generate insights-as-a-service for agriculture (crop identification, yield forecasting, harvest timing), aquaculture (water quality, algal bloom detection, biomass), environment and carbon (sequestration monitoring, deforestation, pollution tracking), and safety and security (vessel detection and tracking, illegal activity warning, rapid change detection). Kuva Space is part of the European Space Agency InCubed-co-funded HYPERFIELD program, was awarded a €1.8M ESA Civil Security from Space contract within the SMART-CONNECT consortium to demonstrate rapid hyperspectral insights for crisis response, and in 2026 signed a Letter of Intent with SSC Space to strengthen Nordic space capabilities. The commercial model is subscription-based insights-as-a-service rather than pay-per-pixel imagery sales, with current access offered through the Kuva Sense Early Adopter Program; the company markets "robust APIs and customizable data formats" for system integration but does not currently publish open public API reference documentation, an OpenAPI specification, or a self-service developer portal. The only public engineering surface is the open-source kuva-data-processing Python toolkit (kuva-metadata, kuva-reader, kuva-geometry) on GitHub and PyPI, which reads Kuva GeoTIFF-based L0/L1AB/L1C/L2A data products and their metadata sidecars.

The clinical pipeline is led by zovegalisib (RLY-2608), described as the first allosteric, pan-mutant, isoform-selective PI3K-alpha inhibitor, in Phase 3 for HR+/HER2- breast cancer and Phase 1/2 for vascular anomalies and PROS; RLY-8161, an NRAS- selective inhibitor, is in Phase 1/2 for NRAS-mutant solid tumors; an alpha-galactosidase A non-inhibitory chaperone for Fabry disease is in discovery; lirafugratinib (RLY-4008, FGFR2) was out-licensed to Elevar Therapeutics in December 2024. Relay has no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release; the Dynamo platform is proprietary internal R&D tooling, and the company's GitHub organization currently has no public repositories. The commercial surface is therapeutic candidates, clinical partnerships, and out-licensing rather than data products.

It builds "the AI company brain" — software that reads everything a company produces (email, chat, documents, CRM, ERP, tickets, meeting notes) and returns findings with citations back to the source. Its products are Noesis (the enterprise flagship company brain built for CEOs, CFOs, and private-equity operating partners), Midas (an AI sales platform that runs inside a company's existing CRM and is paid out of the revenue it produces), and Compendium (shared real-time context and durable memory for engineering and customer-facing teams and their AI agents, including shared Claude Code sessions). The company positions this as the measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV) layer for scalable, verifiable carbon removal, reforestation success tracking, and conservation planning. Coolant raised a $4.3M seed round from General Catalyst and Floodgate in October 2025. As of this profile the company operates a marketing site, a demo web application, and a technical blog, but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Signify Group
companies.description: Signify Group is a London, United Kingdom-based ethical data science firm founded in 2017 by co-founder and CEO Jonathan Hirshler, applying machine learning, natural language understanding, and open-source intelligence (OSINT) to social and digital media data. Its flagship service, Threat Matrix, is widely regarded as the leading platform for detecting, analysing, evidencing, and actioning online abuse and fixated threats directed at athletes, clubs, leagues, player unions, federations, brands, and other public figures. Threat Matrix scans incoming public messages across X (Twitter), Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok in 39+ languages, uses "augmented intelligence" (AI speed combined with trained human analyst nuance) to triage racist, sexist, homophobic, anti-semitic, islamophobic, gambling-driven, and personally targeted abuse, and produces evidence-grade reports with network mapping that can be used by platforms, police, sponsors, and protection teams. Customers and partners include the Professional Footballers' Association (PFA), Kick It Out, the International Tennis Federation (ITF) and WTA Tour covering c.8,300 players, the International Ski and Snowboard Federation (FIS) protecting 1,000+ athletes and officials, the Badminton World Federation (BWF), the NCAA, and Japan's 2026 World Baseball Classic squad. Signify also operates ShareScore (media coverage and social buzz analytics), Sports Insights (fan engagement and athlete insight analytics), and Online Forensics (brand reputation, OSINT investigations, and risk assurance). Signify is a private services firm with no public developer API, no public SDKs, and no public GitHub organization; engagement is via direct sales and managed service contracts with rights-holders, leagues, federations, and enterprise clients.

The company is backed by Sequoia, General Catalyst, Felicis, SoftBank, Bezos Expeditions, and other investors. companies.name: .cursorrules
companies.description: .cursorrules is a project-level configuration file used by the Cursor AI code editor to define custom rules, coding conventions, and behavioral instructions that shape how the editor's AI assistant generates and edits code. The file is placed in the root of a repository and is read automatically by Cursor when the project is opened, giving teams a way to enforce architectural patterns, style guides, framework conventions, and tooling preferences across all AI-generated code. The format is intentionally flexible - rules are typically written in plain Markdown or natural language and may include sections describing project structure, technology stack, naming conventions, testing requirements, and out-of-scope behaviors. Cursor has since extended the concept with .cursor/rules/ directories of multiple scoped rule files, but the original .cursorrules file remains widely used and supported.

Its Chip-on-Diamond and diamond-cooled server products target AI and data-center compute, while its GaN power amplifiers and satellite radios serve space communications, radar, cellular, and automotive/EV markets. Akash Systems is a hardware and materials company with no public developer API or documentation surface; it was surfaced as a DCVC portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

companies.name: Aktoria Robotics
companies.description: Aktoria Robotics is a San Francisco-based robotics company (Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch) building a teleoperation and remote-operation layer for robots under the banner "Human as API for Robots." Its platform lets operators run any robot anywhere in the world, remotely collecting operational data from robot fleets 24 hours a day, monitoring and intervening in deployed fleets, and moving hardware through a train-to-deploy-to-monitor lifecycle. Founded in 2026 by Shreenabh Agrawal (robotics, Carnegie Mellon University) and Jaskaran Singh Walia (previously a researcher at Microsoft, MIT, CMU, Cambridge, and NUS), the company is at the pre-product-launch stage and does not yet publish a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation.

companies.name: Alongside
companies.description: Alongside is an a16z-backed crypto company (alongside.xyz) founded in 2022. It originally launched the Alongside Crypto Market Index (AMKT), the first on-chain broad crypto market index token with a 0% annual fee, backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Coinbase Ventures, and Franklin Templeton. The company has since pivoted to AI-native compliance automation for scaling crypto firms, unifying fragmented KYC/AML/KYT tooling into a single system and reducing manual analyst burden for autonomous financial agents. As of this enrichment pass Alongside publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, MCP server, or developer documentation; this profile captures its identity and probed domain security only.

companies.name: Alterya
companies.description: Alterya is an AI-powered fraud-prevention company founded in 2022 (Y Combinator; seed round led by Battery Ventures, ~$9.8M) that detects authorized-fraud scams — authorized push-payment (APP) scams, pig-butchering and romance scams, money-mule and synthetic accounts, and social-engineering-driven withdrawals — before victims send funds. It connects fraud signals across crypto rails and traditional fiat/bank rails, and prior to acquisition monitored more than $8B in transactions per month for exchanges and fintechs including Binance, Coinbase, and Block, protecting roughly 100M end users. Chainalysis acquired Alterya in January 2025 for a reported ~$150M; it now ships as the "Alterya by Chainalysis" fraud-prevention product. The standalone alterya.com domain is parked and the company operates entirely inside Chainalysis, with no independent public developer portal, API, or OpenAPI surface.

companies.name: Apropose
companies.description: Apropose, Inc. was a Mountain View, California startup spun out of the Stanford University Computer Science Department in 2013 to bring data-driven software to web design. Founded by Ranjitha Kumar, Jerry Talton, Maxine Lim, and Arvind Satyanarayan, the company built tools for large-scale visual page search and web design analytics — letting teams track design trends, compare a site's design against demographics, and surface prevalent design patterns to inject concrete data into the design process. It raised a roughly $1.875M seed round in 2014 led by New Enterprise Associates (NEA) and Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), with angels including Pat Hanrahan and Nick McKeown. The company has since ceased operations and is permanently closed; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation, and its primary domain (apropose.com) is now parked and listed for sale. This profile is retained as an a16z portfolio-lead record.

companies.name: AquaShield
companies.description: AquaShield is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026 / P26 batch) startup building AI-driven water leak detection for buildings and large real estate portfolios. Non-invasive sensors clamp onto existing pipes in minutes with no pipe cutting, retrofits, or downtime; the platform learns each building's normal water-flow patterns and flags anomalies in real time before they escalate into costly damage. Water damage is the largest preventable loss in real estate — more than fire and theft combined. Founded by former MIT and Harvard/EPFL robotics researchers Paul Beckers (CEO) and Marguerite Benoist (CTO), the company is based in San Francisco and works with some of the largest residential portfolios in the world. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; AquaShield currently publishes a marketing site only and does not yet expose a public API or developer program.

companies.name: ArbiLex
companies.description: ArbiLex is a legal-fintech startup founded at the Harvard Innovation Labs in 2018 by Isabel Yang that brings AI and predictive analytics to high-stakes international arbitration and litigation finance. Its Bayesian machine learning and NLP models — trained on a dataset of over nine million cases — produce empirical, explainable case ratings that help counsel quantify uncertainty, reduce errors, and value claims. ArbiLex also operates the ArbiLex Funding Exchange (AFX), a data-driven marketplace pairing AI-rated cases with litigation-finance capital. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global; no public developer API surface was found at time of enrichment.

It was backed by 500 Global, Redwood Ventures, MC Capital, and a Start-Up Chile grant. companies.description: Atrisa (formerly Refortifai) is a Y Combinator (P26) startup building AI agents for analog circuit design. The product is a chat-based assistant engineer that lets hardware and analog design teams ask it, in natural language, to create a design, debug a circuit, or run simulations. Atrisa is designed to fit into existing workflows: teams bring their own toolkit, PDKs (process design kits), and design documents, which Atrisa reads, understands, and adopts to produce schematic-level outputs and iterate on analog designs. As an early-stage company it currently ships a hosted web application rather than a public developer API, so this profile captures its identity, domain-security posture, and public surface pending any future API release.

companies.name: Axelrod
companies.description: Axelrod is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building an autonomous operating layer for boutique, independent, and luxury hotels and resorts. Its software runs daily front-of-house and back-of-house operations, coordinating arrivals, rooms, rates, access, maintenance, supplies, and owner reporting inside the systems and teams a property already has in place, integrating with existing PMS, channel, pricing, and accounting platforms rather than requiring net-new tooling. Founded by Adrian Stoica and Saman Sayahpour, the company markets itself as "boutique hotels that run themselves" and reports being live across four continents with Michelin Key awarded and Marriott Luxury Collection properties. Axelrod does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or documentation; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead.

companies.name: Axon
companies.description: Axon is an early-stage artificial intelligence company building real-time predictive intelligence on a brain-inspired architecture. Its approach centers on small, efficient "world models" that learn continuously on-device rather than depending on large models or the cloud, giving an edge-first design lower latency and lower cost. The initial focus is high-frequency trading and capital markets, where real-time prediction is decisive, with future applications targeted at wearables, edge devices, and robotics. Axon is backed by Northzone, Concept Ventures, a16z Speedrun, and EWOR. As of this profile the company is pre-product with no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or developer portal; this repository tracks it in the API Evangelist network for enrichment as its developer surface emerges.

companies.name: BBN
companies.description: BBN (RTX BBN Technologies, formerly BBN Technologies and Raytheon BBN) is an American research and development organization based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 1948 and now a division of RTX Corporation. BBN has a storied history in computer networking, having built the original ARPANET Interface Message Processors and pioneered early email. Today it delivers advanced technology for national security across AI and machine learning, all-domain command and control, applied biosciences, cyber operations, spectrum dominance, maritime autonomy, multi-domain sensing, resilient networking, planning and logistics, quantum and photonics, and voice and language processing. General Catalyst has backed BBN since 2004. BBN serves government and defense customers and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

companies.description: Talentpluto (Pluto) is an AI voice-agent platform for professional discovery and recruitment, founded in 2025 and part of Y Combinator's Summer 2026 batch out of New York City. The company positions Pluto as a source of truth for career context in an internet increasingly built for agents. Terra AI raised a $20M Series A led by Khosla Ventures with BHP Ventures in June 2026 and serves copper, gold, rare-earth (REE), and reservoir projects. Founded in 2024 by Nathan Nwachuku and Maxwell Maduka, the company builds ArtemisOS (an AI-powered operating system for infrastructure security), the Archer long-range VTOL surveillance drone, the Iroko modular UAV, the Duma autonomous unmanned ground vehicle, and the Kallon solar-powered AI sentry tower to monitor, detect, and respond to threats such as terrorism, sabotage, and armed attacks on critical infrastructure including hydropower plants, mines, and power assets. Terra raised $11.75M led by 8VC in January 2026. As a hardware and defense-systems manufacturer it publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface; this profile is maintained as a company/provider record in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Terranox AI
companies.description: Terranox AI is the first vertically integrated, AI-powered uranium discovery company, founded in 2026 and part of Y Combinator's Winter 2026 batch. The company finds high-grade uranium deposits in North America by training machine learning models on more than seventy years of exploration outcomes locked in thousands of legacy PDFs, drill logs, and hand-drawn geological maps. Traditional uranium exploration has a hit rate below one percent and timelines measured in decades; Terranox aims to raise that hit rate and compress discovery time to help supply the fuel a global nuclear-energy resurgence needs — the world must roughly quadruple uranium production by 2050. Terranox is a private operating company focused on geoscience and mineral exploration and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. It is backed by General Catalyst, 776 Ventures, and Y Combinator.

companies.description: Thistle Technologies provides security tools, libraries, and services for the developers who build connected and embedded devices. Founded by security veteran Window Snyder and backed by DCVC, the company offers a turnkey embedded-device security platform whose two headline products are the Thistle Update Solution (end-to-end over-the-air firmware and software updates for Embedded Linux on ARM/ARM64 and x86-64 as well as Infineon PSoC 6 microcontrollers) and Thistle Secure Boot Enablement (tools and services for enabling secure/verified boot with managed key handling and firmware signing on hardware such as Espressif ESP32, Infineon OPTIGA Trust M secure elements, and U-Boot targets including the Raspberry Pi 4 and BeagleBone). Thistle helps device makers add mechanisms that keep IoT and edge/AI hardware updatable and resistant to compromise without building the security infrastructure themselves. The offering is delivered as SDKs, libraries, and managed services integrated into a customer's device firmware rather than as a public web API.

companies.description: AI VIVO (AIVIVO LTD) is a Cambridge, England based drug-discovery company that combines systems pharmacology with artificial intelligence to accelerate the identification and de-risking of therapeutic candidates. Its "Organome" platform simulates biological processes at the target, cell, organ, and organism levels and ranks drug candidates by their phenotypic effects at the tissue level, without relying on prior knowledge of the disease or compounds. The approach gained recognition in 2020 when the platform ranked roughly 90,000 compounds for COVID-19 and surfaced dexamethasone as a top candidate weeks before its clinical benefit was widely reported. AI VIVO is backed by DCVC and other life-science and applied-AI investors. companies.description: Caption Health was an artificial-intelligence medical-imaging company founded in 2013 and headquartered in San Mateo, California, that built FDA-cleared AI software to guide clinicians through cardiac ultrasound scans in real time. Its flagship products, Caption Guidance and Caption AI, provided real-time image-acquisition guidance, automated image-quality assessment, and automatic ejection-fraction calculation, enabling non-specialist healthcare professionals to capture diagnostic-quality echocardiograms. Backed by DCVC and others (it raised a $53M Series B in 2020), Caption Health was acquired by GE HealthCare in February 2023 for roughly $150M and its technology was absorbed into GE HealthCare's ultrasound portfolio, shipping as Caption AI on the Vscan Air handheld system and within the Verisound AI digital-solutions line. The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public developer API; this profile is retained as a network record of an acquired provider.

companies.name: Endo Health

Describing itself as "the emotional layer of healthcare" and aiming to "make health addictive," the company treats the drivers behind symptoms rather than the symptoms alone, delivering conversational, connection-first care through a mobile health app. Its stated mission is to advance human lifespan by one year. Endo Health is backed by General Catalyst and a16z Speedrun, with teams in San Francisco and Seoul. This is a consumer digital-health product; no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface has been published at this time.

companies.name: Harvest Platform
companies.description: Harvest Platform was a New York City fintech startup founded in 2017 by Gabriel DellAccio and Namrata Baral that built a consumer investing and banking app. Its signature feature used artificial intelligence to identify negotiable bank fees and automatically negotiate refunds with major U.S. banks, later expanding into micro-investing, round-ups, cashback rewards, and savings tooling. The company was backed by Techstars and Financial Venture Studio, raising roughly $3.3M in seed funding. Its domain growmyharvest.com now 302-redirects to Acorns (acorns.com), consistent with reporting that Harvest Platform was acquired by Acorns in 2021. Harvest Platform was a consumer-facing mobile product and never published a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI, so it carries no technical API artifacts.

companies.name: Jungla
companies.description: Jungla, Inc. was a San Francisco precision-medicine informatics startup founded in 2016 by Alexander Colavin and Carlos Araya. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and IndieBio, it built a cloud-based Functional Modeling Platform (FMP), also described as a Molecular Evidence Platform, that combined functional genomics, computational biophysics, cellular engineering, and machine learning to produce auditable predictive models for clinical genetic and genomic variant interpretation. Jungla emerged from stealth in 2018 and was acquired by Invitae Corporation in July 2019 (approximately $59M), where its technology augmented Invitae's Sherloc variant-classification approach. The company is now defunct; its original developer surface (jungla.io) is offline and no public API, documentation, or SDKs survive. This profile is a historical record surfaced from the a16z portfolio; it carries no live developer artifacts.

companies.name: Justinian
companies.description: Justinian is an applied AI company, backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026), building what it calls the first AI-native government affairs firm. Founded by Parth Badhwar (previously Clipbook, The White House, Deloitte's policy team, and the Harris campaign), Justinian helps early-stage companies monitor regulations, lobby policymakers, and win government contracts. The firm operates from San Francisco and Washington, DC, pairing staff drawn from the White House and top lobbying firms with engineering, and frames its mission as rebuilding public-private partnerships in America. Justinian currently presents as a services and product company with a demo-request/contact flow; it does not publish a public developer API, documentation, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

companies.name: Legit Patents
companies.description: Legit (listed by Seedcamp as "Legit Patents", 2016 cohort, legit.ai) was a Cambridge, Massachusetts startup applying natural-language processing to scientific and patent literature, which it developed into an on-demand expert network for the life sciences. Its product let pharmaceutical, biotech and medical-device teams search a corpus the company described as more than two million experts backed by roughly forty million data points, then pay a flat fee per reply to message key opinion leaders directly instead of scheduling calls — marketed for R&D, business development and licensing (BD&L), strategic alliances and integration management. The company is no longer operating: substantive legit.ai content disappears from the web archive after 2021, its LinkedIn company page returns HTTP 404, and the legit.ai domain is now parked on GoDaddy/Afternic and listed for sale (Afternic nameservers, a null MX record and an SPF "-all" policy). No public API, developer portal, documentation or machine-readable specification was ever published; see review.yml for the full probe record.

companies.name: Lumius
companies.description: Lumius is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) medical-imaging startup building fast, smart, accessible real-time 3D ultrasound systems — described as "a 3D camera for the body." The technology aims to move ultrasound beyond traditional 2D imaging to intelligent, AI-assisted 3D visualization across larger volumes, with an initial focus on vascular access and central-line placement (where roughly half of first attempts fail among new clinicians) and future targets including blood-clot detection, tumor diagnosis, and biopsy guidance. The company partners with academic institutions such as Duke University and Columbia University. Lumius is a hardware/device company with no public API, SDK, or developer platform; its products are pre-market and not intended for medical use. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC portfolio lead and has been reviewed by the enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: Manas AI
companies.description: Manas AI is an artificial-intelligence drug-discovery company co-founded by Reid Hoffman and physician-scientist Siddhartha Mukherjee, launched in late 2024 and backed by General Catalyst and Greylock. The company applies machine learning and computational biology to accelerate the discovery and design of new medicines, with an initial focus on hard-to-treat cancers such as breast and prostate cancer and lymphoma. Manas AI operates as a private biotech / therapeutics research organization rather than a developer-facing platform: as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation. This entry is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company profile surfaced from the General Catalyst portfolio.

companies.name: Verge Genomics
companies.description: Verge Genomics (now operating as Verge Labs) is an AI-driven drug discovery biotechnology company using human genomics data and machine learning to discover and develop treatments for neurodegenerative and neuromuscular diseases such as ALS and Parkinson's. Its proprietary all-in-human CONVERGE platform integrates large-scale multi-omic patient datasets derived from human tissue with machine learning to identify novel therapeutic targets, and has been applied in pharmaceutical collaborations with Eli Lilly, AstraZeneca and Alexion. companies.name: .Roorules
companies.description: .roorules is a configuration file convention for Roo Code, an open-source AI-powered autonomous coding assistant built for VS Code. The .roorules file allows developers to define project-specific coding conventions, style rules, architecture guidelines, and behavioral instructions that guide Roo Code AI agents when working within a codebase. Roo Code supports multiple AI providers including Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT-4, Google Gemini, and local LLMs via OpenAI-compatible APIs.

companies.name: 500 Global
companies.description: 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups) is a global venture capital firm and startup accelerator founded in 2010 by Dave McClure and Christine Tsai and headquartered in Palo Alto / Silicon Valley, California. The firm invests from pre-seed to pre-IPO in globally ambitious technology founders, built on the belief that "talent lives everywhere, but capital and opportunity does not." 500 Global pioneered a "lots of little bets" seed strategy, backing hundreds of companies per fund with smaller initial checks, and has grown one of the industry's largest truly global seed portfolios: 3,000+ companies across 80+ countries with $300B+ in cumulative portfolio valuation, including 35+ companies valued at $1B+ and 160+ valued at more than $100M. It runs regional and thematic practices spanning Southeast Asia, Latin America, MENA, Africa, Japan, Korea, Thailand, and Eurasia, plus a Sustainable Growth strategy (health, climate, agriculture, gender, education), flagship accelerator programs, and the VC Unlocked investor-education program that has trained 1,400+ investors. As of April 30, 2025 the firm reported approximately $2.3B in assets under management. Notable investments include Canva, Grab, Talkdesk, Credit Karma, Twilio, and Bukalapak.

companies.name: 8VC
companies.description: 8VC is a technology investment firm founded in 2015 by Joe Lonsdale and Jake Medwell (with founding partners Drew Oetting and Kimmy Scotti) following the wind-down of Formation 8, and headquartered at 907 South Congress Avenue in Austin, Texas after relocating from San Francisco in 2020. The firm both invests in and co-founds early-stage companies, dedicating a significant share of its capital (roughly 25-30%) to building companies from scratch through its "8VC Build" venture-studio program and assembling teams of top specialists. 8VC concentrates on "national capability" and deep-tech categories including defense, life sciences and biotech, healthcare, logistics and supply chain, manufacturing and industrials, enterprise software, financial services, AI, and IT infrastructure. With approximately $6 billion in assets under management (2023) and a public portfolio of more than 170 companies, 8VC is known for its founder-led, mission-driven approach and notable investments including Palantir, Addepar, Anduril, Flexport, Vercel, Saronic, Epirus, Yugabyte, and Project44. The firm runs the 8VC Fellowship and Bio-IT Fellowship talent programs and maintains a stated policy of not accepting capital from foreign-government-connected sources.

companies.name: Accel
companies.description: Accel is one of the world's leading venture capital firms, founded in 1983 by Arthur Patterson and Jim Swartz and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with additional offices in San Francisco, London, and Bangalore, India. Accel describes itself as "the first partner to exceptional teams everywhere," backing founders from seed and early stage through growth worldwide. The firm invests across enterprise software and SaaS, consumer, artificial intelligence, fintech, cybersecurity, infrastructure and developer tools, security, media, and healthcare, and operates dedicated funds for the US, Europe/Israel, and India/Southeast Asia. Accel is known for its "prepared mind" investment philosophy and for backing category-defining companies including Facebook, Slack, Dropbox, Atlassian, CrowdStrike, UiPath, Qualtrics, Spotify, Flipkart, Swiggy, Freshworks, 1Password, Vercel, Scale AI, Anthropic, and Perplexity. Its portfolio spans more than 100 unicorns, dozens of IPOs, and hundreds of acquisitions. In 2024 Accel raised a $650M fund for European and Israeli startups, and in 2025 raised a fund for India and Southeast Asia. This profile tracks Accel's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Addition
companies.description: Addition is a New York City-based venture capital firm founded in 2020 by Lee Fixel, the former head of Tiger Global Management's private equity business. The firm invests in founder-led, technology-enabled companies across multiple stages, allocating roughly one-third of its capital to early-stage investments and the remainder to growth-stage opportunities. Sectors of focus include software and SaaS, fintech and payments, artificial intelligence and machine learning, developer tools and infrastructure, cybersecurity, consumer, logistics, and clean energy. Typical checks range from about $10M to $200M, with a reported sweet spot near $30M-$50M. Addition operates a streamlined solo-GP model with Fixel as sole managing partner making final investment decisions, enabling fast conviction. Across Addition One through Addition Five (2020-2023) the firm raised roughly $7B-$7.3B in committed capital. Notable investments include Stripe, Snyk, Hugging Face, Chainalysis, Navan, dLocal, Delhivery, Airwallex, Freshworks, Warby Parker, and Lyra Health.
